item.title: CAAB dismisses cost rumours, says third terminal to open in December
item.description:
The Civil Aviation Authority of Bangladesh (CAAB) has dismissed what it described as misinformation and rumours surrounding the third terminal of Hazrat Shahjalal International Airport, saying the facility remains on track to begin operations in December.
In a statement issued on Sunday, signed by CAAB spokesperson and Assistant Director (Public Relations) Kawsar Mahmud, the authority urged the public not to be misled by inaccurate reports regarding the project's cost, contract implementation and financial management.
According to the statement, some recent reports in print and electronic media have presented partial or out-of-context information about the project's approved costs, contractual provisions and implementation process, which could create public confusion.
CAAB said that although construction of the terminal was completed nearly two years ago, commercial operations were delayed due to operational readiness, compliance with international technical standards and coordination with relevant stakeholders.
It added that those preparations are now in their final stages and that work is progressing with the goal of launching operations in December, in line with the government's announcement.
The authority warned that misleading information about the project could harm public confidence, damage the country's reputation among international partners and affect preparations for the terminal's launch. It also said such misinformation could negatively impact state revenue and the aviation sector's development.
CAAB also rejected allegations that Tk3,200 crore had been spent on the project without government approval, calling the claim inconsistent with approved project documents and actual expenditure records.
It said all project expenditures require approval from the Planning Commission following recommendations from the Project Implementation Committee (PIC), Project Steering Committee (PSC) and the relevant ministry.
According to CAAB, the project's original Development Project Proposal (DPP), worth Tk13,610 crore, was approved on October 24, 2017. After the procurement process, the first revised DPP, valued at Tk21,399 crore, received government approval on December 10, 2019.
The authority said Tk3,267 crore was later allocated for variation works. However, after adjustments based on actual project requirements, the second revised DPP was approved at Tk21,365 crore—Tk34 crore lower than the previous estimate—on December 7 last year.
CAAB said the project has so far incurred expenditure of Tk20,347 crore, which remains within the approved budget.
It urged all stakeholders to help prevent the spread of rumours and misleading information about the airport project.

item.title: Preliminary registration for Hajj 2027 begins Monday
item.description:
Preliminary registration for Hajj 2027 will begin on Monday and continue until September 24, with intending pilgrims required to complete the process within the stipulated period.
The schedule has been announced in line with the Hajj roadmap issued by Saudi Arabia's Ministry of Hajj and Umrah, the Ministry of Religious Affairs said on Sunday.
Prospective pilgrims will be able to complete primary registration through either the government or private management system by depositing Tk3.5 lakh, it said.
Those who complete primary registration must pay the remaining amount of their selected Hajj package and complete final registration by December 10 this year.
Before primary registration, applicants must complete a pre-registration by depositing Tk30,000, the ministry said.
Under the government arrangement, intending pilgrims can register online by creating an account on the e-Hajj system (hajj.gov.bd).
Registration will also be available through Union Digital Centres, divisional and district offices as well as its Baitul Mukarram office, district and upazila model mosques and the Dhaka Hajj Office.
Pilgrims registering under the government scheme must deposit the required amount at any branch of Sonali Bank using a voucher. Those registering through private Hajj agencies must deposit the money into the agency's designated bank account, the details of which will be available on the Hajj portal.
The ministry also announced several eligibility conditions for Hajj pilgrims.
Children below the age of 15 years will not be allowed to perform Hajj.
People suffering from serious chronic illnesses, including heart, lung, liver or kidney diseases, neurological or mental disorders, dementia, or cancer patients undergoing chemotherapy, biological therapy or radiotherapy, will also be ineligible.
Individuals with active infectious diseases that pose a public health risk, including tuberculosis and haemorrhagic fever, will likewise be barred from performing Hajj.
Women in the final two months of pregnancy or those with high-risk pregnancies will not be issued the required fitness certificate for Hajj.
During primary registration, pilgrims will be required to select their district for Hajj training and vaccination, the type of Hajj and their preferred Hajj package.
Applicants must also possess a passport valid until at least December 31, 2027, the ministry said.
Earlier, on July 21, the government announced two Hajj packages for 2027, setting the cost of maximum Hajj package at Tk615,263 and minimum package at Tk505,648.

item.title: HC issues rule over Tk 50L compensation in St Martin bus crash
item.description:
The High Court has issued a rule asking why Supreme Court lawyer Md Bahauddin Al Imran should not be awarded Tk50 lakh in compensation for injuries he sustained in a Saint Martin Paribahan road accident on the Chittagong-Dhaka Highway.
The court also directed the chairman of the Bangladesh Road Transport Authority (BRTA) Board of Trustees to dispose of Imran's compensation application within 30 days.
In addition, the court issued a rule asking why the route permit and licence of the Saint Martin Paribahan bus involved in the accident (Dhaka Metro B-12-2881) should not be cancelled.
The rule also sought an explanation as to why transport operators should not be directed to comply with prescribed traffic rules, display vehicle fitness certificates prominently and introduce QR codes for verification.
The court further asked why the authorities should not be directed to form rapid response teams comprising police and fire service personnel in accident-prone areas, install 360-degree cameras inside and outside passenger buses to deter reckless driving, and stop the operation of buses converted from single-chassis vehicles.
The order was passed by a High Court bench of Justice Ahmed Sohel and Justice Fatema Anwar on Sunday after a preliminary hearing of the writ petition.
Barrister Sanjid Siddiqui represented the petitioner.
The writ was filed in May by Md Bahauddin Al Imran, who was injured in the accident.
It attached a report published by Bangladesh Pratidin on October 22, 2025, under the headline Aramer Arale Maranphand.
According to the petition, the Dhaka-bound St Martin Paribahan bus, owned by Ifad Motors, left Chittagong on September 19, 2025, and overturned after making a 180-degree turn in the Basantapur area under Chauddagram's Mia Bazar Police Station in Comilla at around 2:05am.
The petition alleged that the driver and his assistant fled the scene after the crash. The bus was left without power, and passengers were rescued with the assistance of police and locals.
Imran sustained multiple injuries, including fractures to five ribs on the left side of his chest, and required prolonged medical treatment and rest, causing him financial loss, according to the petition.
The petitioner said a legal notice was served on the authorities seeking compensation and other remedial measures, but no response was received.
He then filed the writ seeking compensation as well as a series of directives in the public interest aimed at improving road safety.

item.title: Home minister: Shahabuddin's resignation constitutional, no grounds for arrest
item.description:
Home Minister Salahuddin Ahmed on Sunday said former president Mohammed Shahabuddin's resignation was carried out in accordance with the Constitution and the government sees no grounds for his arrest.
He said Shahabuddin enjoyed constitutional immunity while in office and remains entitled to the security and benefits provided to former presidents under the law.
The minister made the remarks while speaking to reporters after an award ceremony honouring police personnel for bravery and outstanding service.
"The president resigned due to physical reasons. He submitted his resignation to the speaker, who accepted it in accordance with the Constitution. As per constitutional provisions, the speaker is now performing the duties of the president on an interim basis," Salahuddin said.
"The entire process was conducted according to the law."
Responding to criticism and protests by political parties over Shahabuddin's resignation, he said: "In post-uprising Bangladesh, everyone has the freedom to express political opinions and make demands. But we have not seen anything that warrants legal action. The president discharged his responsibilities in accordance with the Constitution and cooperated with the government."
He said the Constitution grants the president immunity for actions taken while in office.
"No criminal case can be filed over actions taken during that period. If there are allegations relating to matters outside his official duties, they will be dealt with under the law," he added.
Asked about an alleged leaked audio recording involving Shahabuddin, the minister said the government had only seen reports in the media.
"If any media outlet has published such information, it is for them to establish its authenticity. We have no information on the matter," he said.
Regarding security arrangements for the former president, Salahuddin said Shahabuddin would receive all benefits provided under the law, including Special Security Force (SSF) and President Guard Regiment (PGR) protection for six months, along with additional security from law enforcement agencies as required.
Speaking at the ceremony, the minister said the government would continue rewarding exemplary performance while ensuring accountability for misconduct.
"Those who perform their duties with courage, honesty and sincerity will be recognised. Those who violate the law or obstruct public services will face action," he said.
He said the ceremony was the third of its kind and reflected the government's efforts to build a people-oriented police force following the July uprising.
"We want a police force that meets the expectations of the people. Positive changes are already visible," he added.
Salahuddin alleged that previous political governments had misused law enforcement agencies to retain power, saying the current administration was promoting professional and service-oriented policing instead.
Responding to a question about the absence of police medals during Police Week, the minister said irregularities had been found during the review of the proposed recipients.
"The list is being scrutinised and corrected. Police medals will be awarded very soon," he said.
He praised officers who recently risked their lives to arrest a robber and recover stolen property, as well as police who quickly recovered a lost bag belonging to an expatriate and returned it before the passenger's departure.
"These incidents demonstrate the growing public service mindset within the police," he said.
On allegations of politically backed smuggling at the border, Salahuddin said he had not received any such complaints but assured that any credible allegations would be investigated.
Commenting on the recovery of a suspicious electronic device beneath a Metro Rail pillar during the Rath Yatra, he said the government viewed the timing as coincidental.
"The device was detected due to the vigilance of an Ansar member and later defused by the Bomb Disposal Unit," he said.
Asked about reports of a former US intelligence official staying at Hotel InterContinental Dhaka, he replied: "I am not supposed to know about that. If you have information, publish it, and we will look into it."
On efforts to extradite former inspector general of police Benazir Ahmed from the United Arab Emirates, Salahuddin said Bangladesh had already sent the requested documents and would provide additional information sought by the court within the next couple of days.
Asked about allegations that sniper rifles and 7.62mm ammunition were used during the July-August violence, he said he would comment on the matter in detail at a later time.

Refusal to pay Tk2m in Chattogram: Extortionists vandalise businessman’s building, and detonate crude bombs
item.description:
A group of armed assailants allegedly vandalised a 10-storey building under construction belonging to businessman Mohammad Jasim Uddin and detonated crude bombs (locally known as cocktails) as he refused to pay Tk 2 million in extortion money.

The incident occurred at around 8:00 am on Sunday in a residential area off the Baro Dighirpar–Bhatiary Link Road in Dakkhin Pahartali Ward No. 1 of the Chattogram City Corporation.

According to police and witnesses, eight to ten masked and armed men arrived outside Jasim Uddin’s property in a “tempo” vehicle while construction workers were on site. The attackers entered the building and assaulted the workers before vandalising doors and windows throughout the premises.

During the attack, a construction worker identified as Hasan Saki was allegedly hacked with a machete-like weapon, leaving him injured. Several other workers, including the building’s security guard, were also assaulted. Before fleeing, the attackers detonated three crude bombs at the scene.

Kazi Md Tarek Aziz, Additional Superintendent of Police (Hathazari Circle), told Prothom Alo that investigators had reviewed CCTV footage of the attack.

He said efforts were under way to identify and arrest those responsible.

Mohammad Jasim Uddin, who owns a wholesale rice and sugar business in the Baro Dighirpar area under Hathazari police station, recently began construction of the multi-storey building.

Speaking to Prothom Alo, he alleged, “For the past month, I have been receiving calls from a foreign phone number demanding Tk 2 million in extortion. After the attack on an internet service provider in the city, they remained quiet for a while following the public outcry. However, they resumed calling about a week ago. I immediately informed the police. I will file a case over Sunday’s attack.”

Asked who had threatened him, Jasim Uddin said he did not know their identities.

Local residents claimed that Jasim Uddin’s building was not the only target. They alleged that extortionists had demanded money by telephone from eight to ten other buildings under construction in the Baro Dighirpar area.

According to residents, such organised extortion had never previously occurred in the locality.

The incident follows an attack on 13 July at the office of internet service provider DDN on Chawkbazar Access Road in Chattogram.

A criminal case was filed over that incident, after which Rapid Action Battalion (RAB) and police arrested 20 suspects.

CCTV footage from the earlier attack showed 15 to 20 armed men storming the DDN office, where they vandalised computers, employees’ mobile phones and office furniture using locally made weapons.

One of the attackers was seen in the CCTV footage smashing computer equipment and other property with an axe while the group threatened staff.

The lawsuit alleges that the extortion demand was made by Mobarak Hossain, alias Imon. However, following the incident, an audio recording circulated on Facebook in which a person identifying himself as Imon claimed that his group did not carry out attacks using knives or machetes, adding that “the people of Chattogram know our style of operation.”

item.title: TOP SHOTS (26 July 2026)
Grameenphone and Shikho partner to expand access to digital learning
item.description:
Grameenphone, the country’s leading telecommunications service provider, has partnered with Shikho, one of the most advanced education technology institutions in Bangladesh, to make quality digital education more accessible and affordable for students across Bangladesh, reports a press release.

The agreement was signed recently at GPHouse by Solaiman Alam, chief product officer of Grameenphone, and Shahir Chowdhury, founder & chief executive officer (CEO) of Shikho. Senior officials from both organisations were present at the ceremony.

Attendees from Grameenphone included Yasir Azman, chief executive officer (CEO); Zahiduz zaman, head of Digital Business; Nafees Anwar Choudhury, head of Brand & Market Communications and Skitto; Shomail Ataher, head of Content Business; and Kazi Rashed Abdallah, head of Platform Business. From Shikho, Ishmam Chowdhury, chief operating officer, was also present.

Through this partnership, Grameenphone will bundle Shikho’s premium Mathematics courses into its digital offerings, making them accessible through the MyGP app at discounted rates.

The initiative aims to support students from Class 6 to 10, particularly SSC candidates, while also addressing the needs of parents seeking affordable and reliable academic support.

This will enable students to seamlessly access structured, high-quality academic content in one place. 

Speaking on the occasion, Solaiman Alam, chief product officer at Grameenphone, said, “With the  growing demand for digital learning solutions, this collaboration reinforces Grameenphone’s commitment  to enabling inclusive access to education through technology. Through our partnership with Shikho, we are taking a customer-centric approach by integrating high-quality learning content with connectivity and simplified payment options within MyGP, making Shikho’s premium courses accessible to our 22.3 million monthly active MyGP users. This approach not only makes quality education more accessible and affordable but also enhances customer value and contributes to improved learning outcomes.”

Shahir Chowdhury, founder and CEO of Shikho, said, "Technology only matters when it disappears into the experience. What we are building with Grameenphone is not just integration, it is a simpler way for millions of students to access learning without friction. When discovery, payment, and learning come together in one place, access becomes real. That is how you begin to change things at scale."

item.title: Harvard Academy Scholars Program opens applications, offers $80,000 annual stipend
item.description:
Applications have opened for the Harvard Academy Scholars Program 2027 at Harvard University in the United States. Researchers from any country are eligible to apply for the fully funded programme.

Selected candidates will receive a two-year postdoctoral fellowship at this world's leading higher education institution. Through the Harvard Academy Scholars Program, participants gain the opportunity to work in an international-standard research environment while exchanging ideas with renowned scholars from around the world.

The fellowship provides an annual stipend of USD 80,000. In addition, selected scholars may receive up to USD 6,000 per year in research funding to support their work. Typically, five to six researchers are selected for the fellowship each year.

Researchers from any country may apply. Applicants must have an excellent academic record. Preference will be given to candidates with expertise in foreign languages, international history and different cultures.

Fulbright Scholarship to study in the US at no cost, how to apply

Applicants must complete their PhD after 31 July 2026. Shortlisted candidates will be invited to attend an in-person interview at Harvard in December 2026, with the Harvard Academy covering travel and hotel expenses.

Applicants must submit an online application, along with curriculum vitae (CV), research proposal, writing sample, academic transcripts and three letters of recommendation within the specified deadline.

Benefits of the programme

  • Selected postdoctoral Academy Scholars will receive an annual stipend of USD 80,000.

  • A two-year research opportunity at the Harvard Academy for International and Area Studies.

  • Financial support for research and travel expenses.

  • Access to a range of research-related facilities and resources.

  • Health insurance coverage.

British council offers STEM scholarships for women to study in UK

Application requirements

Applicants must complete the online application form and submit a CV or resume, academic transcripts, a Statement of Research Interests outlining their research plans, one scholarly writing sample and three recommendation letters.

How to apply

Applications must be submitted online through the Harvard Academy Scholars Program website. Applicants are advised to carefully review the eligibility criteria and programme details before applying.

Application deadline: 18 September 2026.

Further details and application instructions are available on the Harvard Academy website.

item.title: No evidence former president spoke to Sheikh Hasina from London: Home minister
item.description:
Home minister Salahuddin Ahmed has said the government has found no evidence to support claims that recently resigned President Mohammed Shahabuddin spoke by telephone with deposed Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina while receiving medical treatment in London.

He said he had seen the reports in newspapers but stressed that the government possessed no information to substantiate them.

He made the remarks today, Sunday, while speaking to journalists in the conference room of the Ministry of Home Affairs at the Secretariat.

The minister added that in the age of the internet, anyone wishing to speak to someone does not need to travel to London and can make a call from Bangladesh.

Allegations have surfaced that Mohammed Shahabuddin spoke by telephone with fugitive Sheikh Hasina while in London for medical treatment.

When asked about the matter, the Home minister said he had only read about it in newspapers.

He added that those concerned should ask the newspapers what evidence they relied on before publishing such a report. He reiterated that the government had no information supporting the allegation.

Opposition parties have demanded the arrest of Mohammed Shahabuddin.

Responding to a question on the issue, the Home minister said, "Ask the opposition why they want the President arrested. Those who are now criticising the President have the right to do so."

He expressed hope that people would continue to enjoy political freedom of expression in the post-uprising period and added that they would also retain the right to protest.

The Home minister further said, "During his tenure as President, including the final period of the authoritarian regime, throughout the tenure of the interim government, and under the current political government, he carried out his duties in accordance with the law and the Constitution. We received the President's cooperation. Under the Constitution, he enjoys constitutional privileges and immunity. No criminal or other legal case can be filed against him in court while that immunity applies. Beyond that, anyone is free to express their views. They may do so, but I do not see anything that warrants serious consideration."

Asked about allegations made against Mohammed Shahabuddin before he became President, the minister said, "If there were any allegations against him at that time, they belong to that period. The matter will proceed in accordance with the law."

Referring to Mohammed Shahabuddin, the Home minister said he would receive all the benefits to which a former President is entitled under the law. He will also receive security protection from the Special Security Force (SSF), the President Guard Regiment (PGR) and other related facilities for six months, along with police and other security support.

When asked about efforts to bring back former Inspector General of Police Benazir Ahmed, the minister said the government was making utmost efforts to secure his return. He added that the Royal Court had requested additional information and that the government would provide the required documents.

Responding to a journalist's question about the recovery of a bomb beneath the Motijheel Metro Rail Station, the Home minister said both the Roth Yatra and Ulto Yatra festivals had concluded smoothly that day.

He said all law enforcement agencies had worked in close coordination to prevent any disorder. He added that he did not believe there was any connection between the explosive device and the religious celebrations organised by members of the Sanatan community.

item.title: Those who left Bangabhaban in silence
item.description:
Md. Shahabuddin is set to depart from Bangabhaban ahead of schedule. His exit from the highest office of the state is largely unceremonious. According to the Constitution, the President is the supreme dignitary of the state. Bangladesh has seen 17 presidents since independence, including Shahabuddin. Among them, two were assassinated while in office, while others served briefly or in acting capacities. However, the majority had to leave their posts before the completion of their tenures.

There is no mandatory state ritual or ceremony prescribed by the Constitution or law for the departure of a president in Bangladesh. However, in 2023, Md. Abdul Hamid was accorded a state farewell at Bangabhaban. At that time, Bangabhaban officials stated that such a formal send-off was a first in the history of independent Bangladesh.

During that event, Abdul Hamid was given a valedictory Guard of Honor. Along with a red-carpet reception, he was bid farewell in a flower-adorned open jeep while petals were showered upon him. When the open jeep reached the main gate of Bangabhaban, Abdul Hamid and his wife proceeded to their private residence in Nikunja in a separate vehicle under the supervision of the Special Security Force.

Even the few Presidents who departed under normal circumstances in Bangladesh did not receive such celebratory send-offs. One reason for this could be that while they were elected during the tenure of their own party, their departure occurred during the tenure of the rival party.

Specifically, between 1991 and 2009, elections were held under neutral caretaker governments. Each time, the opposition party formed the government, meaning the incumbent party lost the election and took the opposition benches.

Consequently, no efforts were made to commemorate the departure of a president elected by the opposing party.

The now-banned Awami League abolished the caretaker government system back in 2011. Subsequently, three elections were held in 2014, 2018 and 2024, keeping the ousted Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina's government in power. It was predetermined before the elections that the Awami League would win and Sheikh Hasina would become the Prime Minister. Every election during that era was controversial.

During Sheikh Hasina's long fifteen and a half year reign, Bangladesh saw three presidents. The first president, Zillur Rahman, passed away in 2013. Later the then-Speaker Abdul Hamid took over as acting president. He was subsequently elected president twice in a row. According to the Constitution of Bangladesh, no one can serve as president for more than two terms.

In 2023, Md. Shahabuddin became president somewhat unexpectedly. It was during his tenure in 2024 that a fictitious election was held involving Awami League, its affiliate parties and independent Awami League candidates.

On August 5 of that year, Sheikh Hasina's government was ousted in a student-led mass uprising. Sheikh Hasina fled to India. Following this, it became largely certain that Md. Shahabuddin might not be able to complete his presidential term. After a year and a half under the interim government, following the BNP's victory in the election and its formation of the government, the countdown for Shahabuddin to vacate the presidency began. The moment came to pass last Friday.

Early crises and assassinations

The first president of Bangladesh was Bangabandhu Sheikh Mujibur Rahman. However in his absence, Syed Nazrul Islam served as the acting president. Bangabandhu assumed the office of president after returning to independent Bangladesh from imprisonment in Pakistan on 10 January 1972. Two days later, on 12 January, the presidential system was abolished and a parliamentary system of government was introduced. Bangabandhu assumed the role of Prime Minister, and Justice Abu Sayeed Chowdhury became the president.

He served until 24 December, 1973. Later, the then-Speaker Mohammadullah assumed the responsibilities of acting president. On 27 January 1974, he took office as the elected president. Following the establishment of BAKSAL on 25 January 1975, Bangabandhu Sheikh Mujibur Rahman reassumed the presidency the following day. On 15 August of that year, a group of army personnel brutally assassinated Bangabandhu along with his family.

Following the assassination of Bangabandhu, Khondaker Mostaq Ahmad became the president. During this period, coups and counter-coups continued. Within three months, Mostaq was forced to relinquish power. He handed over the power to the then-Chief Justice Abu Sadat Mohammad Sayem. On 29 November 1976, Ziaur Rahman became the Chief Martial Law Administrator. Ziaur Rahman became the president after Abu Sadat Mohammad Sayem resigned on 21 April 1977.

Ziaur Rahman took office as the elected president in June 1978. On 30 May 1981, Zia was killed by a group of army personnel at the Chittagong Circuit House. Following this, the then-Vice President Justice Abdus Sattar assumed the role of acting president and was later elected president.

Meanwhile, the then-Army Chief HM Ershad appeared on the scene. Ershad seized power through a bloodless coup in 1982. After nine consecutive years of movements and struggles, Ershad was forced to hand over power to the interim government of Justice Md. Shahabuddin Ahmed on 6 December, 1990.

Departures under opposing regimes

After BNP won the 1991 election and the parliamentary system of government was reintroduced, the presidency became a largely ceremonial role. BNP’s Abdur Rahman Biswas became the president. Although he completed his full term, he did not receive a farewell reception. By the time of his departure, the Awami League had come to power following the 1996 election.

When the Awami League first came to power under Sheikh Hasina’s leadership in 1996, Justice Shahabuddin Ahmed became the president. However, his relationship with the Awami League government later turned bitter after the party’s defeat in the 2001 election. Sheikh Hasina and other Awami League leaders alleged that their elected president, Shahabuddin Ahmed, had not played a ‘proper’ role during the polls. Following the BNP's return to power, Justice Shahabuddin’s departure took place in near-total silence and seclusion.

Following the fall of the Ershad regime, the then-Chief Justice Shahabuddin Ahmed had assumed the role of acting president at the request of political parties, including the Awami League and BNP, to form an interim government. An election involving all parties was held under that administration. Shahabuddin Ahmed is remembered with respect in the country's political and social spheres.

Justice Shahabuddin Ahmed had to assume the presidency during a period of crisis. He remains a respected figure across the country's political and social landscapes.

In 2001, the BNP-Jamaat alliance government elected party leader A.Q.M. Badruddoza Chowdhury as president. However, he was forced to vacate the office after only seven months and seven days. He was asked to resign following disagreements with the party.

After Badruddoza Chowdhury’s resignation, the then-Speaker Muhammad Jamiruddin Sircar served as acting president. In September 2002, the BNP government elected Professor Iajuddin Ahmed as president.

When the term of Khaleda Zia’s government ended on 28 October, 2006, a crisis emerged regarding who would head the caretaker government. Amidst the deadlock, President Iajuddin Ahmed assumed the role of Chief Advisor himself and formed an interim government.

The Awami League and other opposition parties launched a movement against him. Eventually, a military-backed caretaker government was formed through the political shift known as ‘One-Eleven’ (1/11). However, Iajuddin remained in the presidency. After the Awami League formed the government following the 2008 election, Zillur Rahman became the president.

item.title: Former President Shahabuddin has left Bangabhaban
item.description:
A day after resigning from the position of president, Md Shahabuddin along with his family has left Bangabhaban, today, Sunday at 2: 25 PM.

The motorcade of the former president was seen leaving Bangabhaban.

The motorcade included 18 vehicles, including the president's car and those from law enforcement agencies.

Starting from the afternoon, various media personnel were waiting in front of Bangabhaban. Curious onlookers also gathered on the street in front of Bangabhaban. Since the afternoon, law enforcement personnel were seen to be active in front of Bangabhaban.

At Md Shahabuddin's residence on Road 123 in Gulshan, cleaning work is underway. It was observed on Saturday, that the seating area on the ground floor of the house has been freshly painted. Furniture is being cleaned. Before becoming president, Md Shahabuddin used to live in the apartment on the fifth floor of the house.

Security has been tightened at the former president's Gulshan residence as well. Since morning, members of the police, RAB, and other law enforcement agencies have been present there.

After leaving Bangabhaban, Acting President Hafiz Uddin Ahmad will carry out official duties there. However, he will stay at the official residence of the Speaker of the National Parliament.

Last Friday afternoon, Md. Shahabuddin sent his signed resignation letter to the Speaker of the National Parliament, Hafiz Uddin Ahmad.

Upon receiving the resignation, the Speaker announced the matter at a press conference in the oath room of the Parliament building.

Simultaneously, according to the constitution, the Speaker declared that he would assume the responsibilities of the president.

Md. Shahabuddin vacated the presidential post almost two years before his term was to end, citing illness as the reason for his resignation.

Md. Shahabuddin was elected unopposed as the 22nd president of the country on 24 April 2023, through the nomination of the Awami League.

The presidential term is five years, which means his term was supposed to end in April 2028. However, he is leaving Bangabhaban about 21 months before the end of his term.

item.title: Why children are no longer safe with people they know
item.description:
A seven-month-old baby girl was allegedly killed by her father in Dhaka's Turag area on July 16, while four days later, a nine-year-old girl in Satkhira was allegedly strangled to death by a neighbor seeking to steal her gold earrings.
Though the incidents occurred separately, child rights advocates say they reflect a growing pattern of children falling victim to violence at the hands of people they know and trust.
Recent incidents have reinforced these concerns. In March, an eight-year-old child in Sitakunda, Chittagong, was allegedly abducted by a neighbor who attempted to rape the child before killing them. Another eight-year-old in Dhaka's Pallabi area was raped and murdered. In both cases, the accused were known to the victims and their families.
According to Ain o Salish Kendra (ASK), a total of 2,776 children were killed in Bangladesh between January 2021 and June 2026—an average of 42 child deaths every month. During the same period, 474 children were killed within their own families, while 566 died after being physically abused. ASK also documented at least 4,311 children who experienced 20 different forms of violence.
In the first six months of 2026 alone, 195 children were killed. Among them, 76 were aged between 13 and 16, while 49 were between seven and 12, and 61 were under six years old. Only 59 cases were filed in connection with the killings, raising concerns about accountability and access to justice.
ASK recorded 596 child killings in 2021; 516 in 2022; 485 in 2023; 574 in 2024; and 410 in 2025. Although the annual figures fluctuated, experts said the nature of the crimes had become increasingly severe, including rape followed by murder, domestic violence resulting in death, kidnapping, abuse of child house helps, and sexual violence by trusted adults.
Data from Human Rights Support Society (HRSS) showed that 291 children experienced violence in June 2026 alone. Among them, 54 died, 237 suffered physical or psychological abuse, and 75 were victims of rape. Human rights organizations believe the actual number is higher because many incidents go unreported due to social stigma, family pressure, fear of retaliation, and limited confidence in the justice system.
Experts said violence against children stems from multiple social, economic, and psychological factors, including family conflict, poverty, unemployment, substance abuse, mental health challenges, and weak child protection systems. Many cases occur after prolonged abuse within the home.
Psychiatrist Dr Bulbul Ahmed Khan said: "Exposure to domestic violence affects brain development, lowers self-confidence, creates fear and insecurity, and increases the risk of depression, anxiety, post-traumatic stress disorder, suicidal behavior, and violent tendencies later in life. Domestic violence is not only a family issue; it is also a major public health concern."
Child protection organizations also noted that many families avoid discussing body safety, personal boundaries, and the concepts of "good touch" and "bad touch," leaving children unable to recognize abuse or reluctant to report it.
Professor Rasheda Nasir of the Department of Sociology at the University of Dhaka said rapid urbanization, the decline of extended families, the rise of nuclear households, online addiction, drug abuse, and violent digital content had created new risks for children.
She said: "Many children now spend long hours without adequate adult supervision or are left in the care of house helps, relatives, or neighbors, making them more vulnerable to abuse. At the same time, social media and online games have increased children's exposure to cyber grooming, blackmail, and online sexual exploitation."
Professor Sumaiya Iqbal of the Department of Criminology at the University of Dhaka said child abuse was driven by multiple interconnected factors, including family conflict, poor parental mental health, substance abuse, poverty, unemployment, financial stress, and limited awareness of children's rights.
She said legal punishment alone could not solve the problem and added: "Preventing child abuse requires positive parenting, families that listen to children, and zero tolerance for physical or emotional violence. Schools should strengthen child protection education, while families facing domestic violence, addiction, mental health challenges, or severe financial hardship should receive timely social and government support. Communities must also play a stronger role in identifying risks before children become victims."
Advocate Sifat Nahar said violence against children was not only a criminal offense but also a violation of fundamental human rights. She said: "Every place where a child spends time, including the home, school, and workplace, must be safe."
She added: "Every allegation of child abuse should be investigated promptly and impartially, and offenders must face fair trials and appropriate punishment. Child protection must be treated as a national priority through coordinated efforts involving families, schools, law enforcement agencies, local government institutions, social service providers, and civil society."
Bangladesh has enacted several laws and policies to protect children, including the Children Act 2013, the Women and Children Repression Prevention Act, 2000, and its commitments under the UN Convention on the Rights of the Child (UNCRC).
However, child rights organizations argue that weak implementation, slow investigations, and lengthy judicial processes continue to undermine these protections.
Experts said justice alone would not be enough to prevent child abuse. They stressed that every case should be examined to identify its underlying causes and prevent similar incidents in the future.
Md Saifullah, PPM, assistant inspector general (Crime Analysis), urged parents and guardians to report suspected child abuse immediately. He said: "Parents should stay involved in their children's daily lives, pay close attention to both their online and offline activities, and work with local communities to help create a safer environment for children."
The deaths of the infant in Turag, the child in Satkhira, and hundreds of other children across Bangladesh highlight broader concerns over child safety.
Experts say protecting children requires positive parenting, effective enforcement of child protection laws, quality education, stronger community support, timely justice, and a culture in which children are heard, respected, and protected.

State minister seeks stronger Bangladesh-IFRC partnership on climate resilience
item.description:
State Minister for Foreign Affairs Shama Obaed Islam on Sunday underscored the importance of enhanced collaboration between the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and IFRC in advancing climate resilience initiatives with special attention to women and children.

She appreciated the IFRC’s longstanding partnership with Bangladesh since the Liberation War and its valuable contributions to emergency response and humanitarian assistance.
The state minister particularly expressed appreciation for the IFRC’s sustained support during natural disasters, including floods, cyclones and other climate-induced emergencies as well as its assistance to the Rohingya humanitarian response.

Jatiya Party's expenditure exceeds income in 2025
item.description:
Jatiya Party, led by GM Quader, spent more than it earned during the 2025 calendar year, according to the party's annual financial statement submitted to the Election Commission (EC) on Sunday.
The party reported an income of Tk1,82,04,270 and an expenditure of Tk1,87,93,433, resulting in a deficit of Tk5,89,163 for the year.
Jatiya Party Additional Secretary General Rezaul Islam Bhuiyan submitted the income and expenditure statement for 2025 to EC Senior Secretary Akhtar Ahmed at the Nirbachan Bhaban in Agargaon.
Speaking to reporters after submitting the statement, Rezaul said the party's total income until December 31, 2025, stood at Tk18,204,270, while total expenditure amounted to Tk1,87,93,433.
He said the party had Tk2,66,55,164 in its bank accounts, including the previous year's balance, and after meeting all expenditures, the closing bank balance stood at Tk78,61,731.
Rezaul attributed the higher expenditure to election-related activities during the year.
Referring to the upcoming local government elections, he said political parties will not be able to contest officially under party symbols this time, but Jatiya Party-backed candidates will participate independently with the party's support.
Asked about demand for legal action against former president Mohammed Shahabuddin following his recent resignation, the Jatiya Party leader said: “The question is whether he engaged in any unconstitutional activities while in office. If he did not, why should we demand his arrest? The Jatiya Party has no comment on the issue."
Responding to a question about the impact of divisions within the party following the fall of the Awami League government, he claimed that most leaders who had left the party since have returned under GM Quader's leadership.
Rezaul expressed optimism that Jatiya Party-backed candidates will perform well in the upcoming local government elections, particularly in certain regions, and said the previous split had not significantly affected the party's grassroots organization.
He also hinted at the possibility of the party's divided factions being reunited in the future.

Law minister calls for working together to establish an accountable state system, rule of law
item.description:
Emphasizing the government’s firm position on corruption, Law, Justice and Parliamentary Affairs Minister Advocate Md Asaduzzaman said that the judiciary, legal professionals, and state institutions must collaborate to uphold the rule of law and create a system of accountability.
He encouraged the new generation of lawyers to adopt a resolute approach against corruption, urging them to utilize their talents, integrity, and professional abilities to promote justice.
"The present government aims to move away from the previous culture of theft and money laundering, striving to establish a transparent, accountable, and democratic state. To achieve this, it is essential to enforce the rule of law at all societal levels and foster a united front against corruption," he said while speaking as the chief guest at the opening of a training workshop for newly admitted lawyers at the Chittagong District Bar Association auditorium on Sunday.
A total of 1,054 newly enrolled lawyers took part in this workshop organized by the Chittaagong District Bar Association. The programme focused on the social standing, professional ethics, and the crucial role of lawyers in upholding justice.
During the event, Law Minister Advocate Md Asaduzzaman highlighted the alarming extent of corruption under the previous authoritarian government, saying: “In the last 16 years, $234 billion have been smuggled out of Bangladesh; this information is not mine, but is published in the renowned “Time Magazine.”
“This means that approximately 16 billion dollars have left the country each year, which is equivalent to two or three of the current budgets,” he said. For example, he said: “Tk280 crore was designated for the construction of a 4.5-kilometer road in Khulna, and during the regime of an individual referred to as “Maharaj” in Pirojpur, work valued at Tk3,500 crore was embezzled, merely documented on paper and pen within the LGED department. At that time, the citizens of the country endured a period when corruption had become institutionalized across nearly all sectors.”
The law minister advised the new lawyers that there are no shortcuts to becoming a lawyer. Continuous learning is essential, he said, encouraging them to serve the public, uphold justice, and maintain professional integrity without pursuing wealth.
Following the event, Law Minister Md Asaduzzaman responded to inquiries from journalists regarding former president Md Sahabuddin, stating: “The government is currently examining the various allegations made against him during his tenure as the chairman of the Anti-Corruption Commission (ACC)”.
“In response to public demand, appropriate actions will be taken in accordance with the law after a thorough investigation of the allegations, as the government is committed to ensuring that no individual is subjected to unjust treatment. Nevertheless, a decision will be made based on legal principles after confirming the veracity of the claims,” he said.
The event was chaired by Tarique Ahmed, president of the Chittagong District Bar Association, and Chittagong City Corporation Mayor Dr Shahadat Hossain, MP Abu Sufian, District and Sessions Judge Kazi Abdul Hannan, Metropolitan Sessions Judge Md Hasanul Islam, Chief Metropolitan Magistrate AGM Monirul Hasan Sarkar, Chief Judicial Magistrate Md Sohag Talukder, Deputy Commissioner and District Magistrate Mohammad Zahidul Islam Miah, and Bangladesh Bar Council Ad Hoc Committee Member Mohammad Nazim Uddin Chowdhury, among others, addressed the function.
The event was facilitated by Mohammad Nazrul Islam, deputy general secretary of the Chittagong District Bar Association, while General Secretary Mohammad Moinuddin delivered the welcome address.

item.title: Man to die for killing elderly woman in Narayanganj
item.description:
A Narayanganj court on Sunday sentenced a man to death for killing a 77-year-old woman and stealing her gold jewelry in Rupganj in 2021. Judge Md Abu Shamim Azad of the Narayanganj District and Sessions Judge Court delivered the verdict, also imposing an additional 10 years of rigorous imprisonment for robbery, along with fines totaling Tk 250,000.
The convict, Md Rubel Mia, also known as Rubel Pradhan, was present in court during the judgment.
According to the prosecution, Rubel entered the victim Shafia Begum’s house on January 22, 2021 and fatally attacked her with a sharp weapon before fleeing with a gold chain and earrings.
The victim’s daughter later filed a murder and robbery case with Rupganj Police Station. Police submitted the charge sheet in June 2023, and Rubel later confessed before a magistrate under Section 164 of the Code of Criminal Procedure.
Prosecutors said the murder was motivated by Rubel’s need for money to buy drugs. The court delivered the verdict after examining testimony from 12 prosecution witnesses.

item.title: Complaint lodged with ICT against 28 cultural figures over July uprising killings
item.description:
The State Dialogue Forum (SDF) on Sunday filed a complaint with the International Crimes Tribunal (ICT), accusing 28 prominent figures from Bangladesh's cultural sector of alleged involvement in crimes committed during the July 2024 mass uprising.
Al Noor Mohammad Ayas, central member secretary of SDF, submitted the complaint to ICT Chief Prosecutor Md Aminul Islam.
Those named in the complaint include actors Ferdous Ahmed, actress and filmmaker Meher Afroz Shaon, actors Riaz Ahmed, Aruna Biswas, Shomi Kaiser, Rokeya Prachy, Mahiya Mahi, Nipun Akter, Tanvin Sweety, Hridi Haq, Jyotika Jyoti, Saju Khadem, Sohana Saba, model and lawyer Pia Jannatul, Shamima Tusti, Hero Alom, Ashna Habib Bhabna, Simon Sadik, Sujata Azim, Zayed Khan, Azizul Hakim, Chandan Reza, Asaduzzaman Noor, model Maria Kispatta, journalists Anis Alamgir, Soma Islam, Shanta Farzana and political leader Momin Mehedi.
In the complaint, SDF alleged that the accused were involved in crimes against humanity committed during the July uprising, including incitement to genocide, aiding and abetting, instigation and other related offences.
The organisation said it had filed the complaint seeking an impartial, transparent and lawful investigation by the ICT into the allegations.
Speaking to reporters after submitting the complaint, Ayas alleged that several of those named, including Shanta Farzana and Momin Mehedi, had continued to disparage the July mass uprising.
He claimed that the Awami League government's fall on August 5 marked the end of its rule and alleged that some of its supporters were attempting to re-enter public life as lawyers or academics. He said the organisation would oppose such efforts.

item.title: SDF seeks ICT probe into Shahabuddin's alleged role in July killings
item.description:
The State Dialogue Forum (SDF) has submitted a petition to the International Crimes Tribunal, seeking an investigation into the alleged role of former president Mohammed Shahabuddin in the killings during the July 2024 mass uprising, as well as enforced disappearances and torture during the Awami League's rule.
The petition was submitted to the Chief Prosecutor on Sunday by the forum's central member secretary, Al Noor Mohammad Ayas.
In the petition, Ayas alleged that he was abducted by masked men from the Mohakhali bus terminal on the night of January 18, 2025, after leading protests at Shahbagh demanding Shahabuddin's resignation. He claimed he was subjected to physical and psychological torture and was forced to record a video message calling for the suspension of the movement.
According to the petition, he was abandoned near the Kawran Bazar-Banglamotor area the following day and was later rescued and admitted to Dhaka Medical College Hospital.
Ayas also urged the tribunal to investigate Shahabuddin's alleged role as an instigator of the shootings, killings, enforced disappearances and other alleged human rights abuses against students and civilians during the July 2024 mass uprising.
He further called for an impartial and independent investigation into Shahabuddin's constitutional role and responsibilities as the then president, as well as whether he bore any legal liability or involvement in the 2024 election, alleged human rights violations, and events related to the mass uprising.

item.title: Bangladeshi artist wins gold prize at World Beauty Art & Design International Contest
item.description:
Bangladeshi artist Sayma Sadia won the gold prize in the Makeup – General Category at the 25th World Beauty Art & Design International Contest, held in Seoul, South Korea.
Organized by the World Beauty Art Association, the annual competition brings together beauty artists, educators, and professionals from around the world to showcase their work in makeup, beauty, and artistic design.
According to officials at the award ceremony, Sayma received the gold prize in recognition of her artistic skill, creativity, and technical expertise in the Makeup – General Category.
Sayma is currently pursuing a bachelor's degree in Beauty Design at Woosong University in South Korea. She said the award marked a significant milestone in her career and encouraged her to pursue higher goals in the global beauty industry.
She hopes to work with internationally recognized beauty and cosmetics brands while specializing in Special Effects (SFX) Makeup, a field widely used in film, television, fashion, and theater.
Speaking about the achievement, Sayma said: “I feel deeply honored and grateful to receive this recognition. Winning the gold prize is not just my achievement, it belongs to everyone who has supported me throughout my journey. At this moment, I especially remember my parents and my sister, whose love, encouragement, and sacrifices have helped me reach this stage. Their belief in me has always been my greatest strength.”
Her achievement reflects the growing presence of Bangladeshi talent in international beauty and design competitions and highlights the country's expanding participation in the global creative industry.

item.title: Flash flood at northwest China tourist site kills 10, injures 23
item.description:
A flash flood caused by heavy rain struck a tourist site in northwest China on Sunday, killing 10 people and injuring 23, state media reported.
“A mountain torrent triggered by short-term heavy rainfall at a scenic spot in Weiyuan County, Dingxi City, trapped some campers” at the location in Gansu Province, state broadcaster CCTV said.
An earlier report by CCTV identified the location of the flash flood as the Shuangshimen Scenic Area in the rugged, mountainous stretches of southern Gansu—roughly 1,200 kilometers southwest of Beijing.
Shuangshimen is known for its natural stone arches, alpine meadows, and mountain streams. It is a popular summer camping spot.
“The injured have been sent to the hospital for treatment, and another 174 people have been rescued,” CCTV said.
Large swaths of southern China are on high alert for floods on Sunday after Typhoon Noul made landfall early in the morning.
Parts of Gansu -- far from Noul’s path -- also experienced heavy rainfall on Sunday, with local authorities across the province issuing weather alerts.

Anusheh Anadil says she is gradually losing her hearing
item.description:
Singer Anusheh Anadil has revealed that a worsening hearing condition is the reason she quietly stepped away from music at the height of her career.
Known for her renditions of songs such as “Tomar Ghore” and “Ghate Lagiya Dinga”, Anusheh had long been absent from concerts, leaving fans wondering why she no longer performed.
Addressing the speculation, the singer said she has been gradually losing her hearing because of tinnitus, a condition that has made performing increasingly difficult.
"I just wanted to be honest about why I no longer sing," she said.
"I am slowly losing my ability to hear. I have something called tinnitus. And the noise in my ear is so loud that I can no longer stand loud noises. It literally hurts my ears."
Anusheh said doctors advised her to use hearing aids, but she felt they worsened her condition.
"The doctors asked me to wear hearing aids, but that dependency is making me hear even less and my tinnitus worse. So I stopped wearing them," she explained.
She added that the condition has also reshaped her lifestyle, leading her to seek a quieter environment away from the city.

Bangladesh's drowning prevention efforts praised
item.description:
The World Health Organization (WHO) offered several reasons for choosing Ghana as the venue for launching the upcoming global report outlining what member states should do to prevent drowning.

One reason is that this West African country has a disproportionately high drowning rate relative to its population. Another is to highlight what African policymakers are doing to tackle this major cause of preventable death.

Policymakers, researchers and development practitioners from around the world gathered in Accra, the capital of Ghana, for a three-day international conference to explore what works in preventing drowning.

At various sessions of the conference, organised by the World Health Organization (WHO), one country's name came up repeatedly—Bangladesh.

The reason is that the two community-based interventions now recongnised globally as the most effective measures for preventing drowning were first proven effective on a large scale in Bangladesh.

25 July marks World Drowning Prevention Day. This year's theme is "Unite to turn the tide." The global report launched at the conference presents seven strategies for drowning prevention and emphasises the need for coordinated, multisectoral action.

Bangladesh's experience was highlighted in many of the presentations as a model for other countries. Ironically, however, while the world is now looking to Bangladesh's experience for guidance, the initiatives have repeatedly stalled within Bangladesh itself due to a lack of political and administrative continuity.

The examples from Bangladesh

At least two of the most effective strategies for drowning prevention were developed by the Centre for Injury Prevention and Research, Bangladesh (CIPRB).

In 2005, a study by CIPRB found that children aged two to five years account for the highest number of drowning deaths in Bangladesh.

Most of these incidents occur between 9:00am and 2:00pm, when parents are busy with work and children are left unsupervised.

The study demonstrated that keeping children in community-based daycare centres during these hours and making nearby water bodies safe by fencing or installing barriers could significantly reduce drowning deaths.

Based on this evidence, the World Health Organization (WHO) incorporated these two interventions into its Global Technical Package for Drowning Prevention.

CIPRB successfully implemented these interventions in 51 unions across Bangladesh. It established a total of 3,205 community daycare centres, reaching 116,054 children aged 9 to 47 months. During the implementation period, the rate of child drowning in those intervention areas declined significantly.

The world learned from Bangladesh

UNICEF supported CIPRB's evidence-based research. However, the initiative did not continue because it received no further government support. Even so, many countries around the world have drawn on Bangladesh's experience in developing their own drowning prevention programmes.

One of the participants at the conference in Ghana was Onyum Charles Okao, Media and Communications Consultant at the international organisation Global Health Incubator. Although he has never visited Bangladesh, the Ugandan national first learned about the country while working on drowning prevention.

Speaking to Prothom Alo, he said, “In Bangladesh, children aged two to five are the biggest victims of drowning. The situation is different in Uganda. Here, children in that age group account for 11 per cent of drowning deaths, while people aged 15 to 30 account for 38 per cent. However, when we started our work in Uganda, Bangladesh's experience played an extraordinary role in building our knowledge base.”

Huyen Doan, a representative of the Global Health Advocacy Incubator (GHAI) in Vietnam, said, “There is much the world can learn from Bangladesh's experience in preventing drowning deaths. That was one of the key lessons that emerged from our discussions."

She said that eight years ago, around 2,000 children aged between six and nine drowned every year in Vietnam. Now, the national drowning rate has fallen by 10 per cent. In the areas where their programme is being implemented, the rate has declined by 16 per cent.

In the Indian state of West Bengal, drowning—particularly child drowning—remains a major public health problem. Although there is no comprehensive government survey, data from non-governmental organisations suggest that more than 9,000 children drown there every year. The Sundarbans region is considered the most at risk.

Meghendra Banerjee, Chief Programme Officer of the Child in Need Institute (CINI), which works on child safety in West Bengal, told Prothom Alo, “Bangladesh’s experience in preventing drowning has now become a global issue. We have learned a great deal from Bangladesh. We have also drawn on the experiences of other Indian states. However, there is no reason to overlook Bangladesh’s achievements.”

Lack of continuity

Despite receiving international recognition, Bangladesh has failed to maintain continuity in its drowning prevention efforts.

At a time when drowning deaths had reached alarming levels, the Bangladesh Shishu Academy, under the Ministry of Women and Children Affairs, launched the Integrated Community-Based Centre for Child Care, Protection and Swim-Safe Facilities (ICBC) project. The first phase of the project ran from 2022 to 2025 across 45 upazilas in 16 districts.

Several non-governmental organisations were assigned to implement the project. According to the project evaluation report, each organisation worked with 25,000 children. The report found that child deaths in those programme areas were almost negligible.

In May this year, Minister for Women and Children Affairs AZM Zahid Hossain told Prothom Alo that the project would be relaunched in 30 districts by adding 14 more districts to the existing coverage.

Al-Amin Bhuiya, a researcher at the Centre for Injury Prevention and Research, Bangladesh (CIPRB), told Prothom Alo that drowning prevention cannot succeed if treated as an isolated initiative of a single ministry or department.

Instead, he said, it requires a coordinated effort involving all relevant ministries, including health, local government, education, women and children affairs, and other related agencies.

item.title: Why govt withdraws police escorts for 18 ministers
item.description:
Eighteen cabinet members who have travelled under police escort in the capital since taking office will now have to travel without such protection.

The government has decided to withdraw the police escort vehicles that previously accompanied them while moving in Dhaka. From now on, only six ministers and one adviser with the rank of minister will continue to receive the facility.

The information was confirmed by multiple sources within the Ministry of Home Affairs and the Dhaka Metropolitan Police (DMP).

According to those sources, the decision was implemented by the DMP on the instruction of the home minister, following the prime minister’s directive.

However, all ministers will continue to receive police protection and security arrangements, where necessary, during official visits outside the capital.

The ministers who will continue to receive police escorts in Dhaka are Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir, Minister for Local Government, Rural Development and Cooperatives; Salahuddin Ahmed, Minister of Home Affairs; Amir Khasru Mahmud Chowdhury, Minister of Finance and Planning; Professor AZM Zahid Hossain, Minister for Social Welfare and Women and Children Affairs; Khalilur Rahman, Minister of Foreign Affairs; Iqbal Hasan Mahmud, Minister for Power, Energy and Mineral Resources; and Rashed Al Mahmud Titumir, Adviser for Planning with the rank of minister.

Officials, however, have not provided a clear explanation of the security assessment or criteria under which these seven office-holders continue to receive the escort facility.

Several senior police officers told Prothom Alo that the arrangements had been retained on the basis of operational necessity.

The police vehicle travelling ahead of a minister's official vehicle is known as an escort or protection vehicle.

According to sources in the DMP's Protection Division, each vehicle is staffed by a five-member police team, which accompanies the minister according to his or her official schedule within the capital.

Police sources said that the withdrawal of escort facilities for 18 ministers has resulted in the redeployment of around 90 police officers.

Previously, approximately 120 officers had been assigned to ministerial escort duties; that number has now fallen to 30–35 officers. The number of escort vehicles has also been reduced from 25 to seven, with the freed personnel and vehicles reassigned to other policing responsibilities.

Why the sudden decision?

Officials familiar with the matter said the decision was not driven by a single factor. Rather, according to sources in both the home ministry and the police, it reflects a combination of considerations.

These include fuel conservation, a shortage of police vehicles, and the government's policy of reducing the size of official motorcades. The prime minister’s own decision to scale back his security convoy is also said to have influenced the move.

Officials believe the measure will additionally help ease traffic congestion in the capital.

According to several government officials, the prime minister’s convoy previously included two police protocol vehicles, but he has now dispensed with them. His principal security continues to be provided by the Special Security Force (SSF).

The police now provide only a motorcycle pilot escort, consisting of four officers travelling on motorcycles—two in front and two behind the motorcade.

Mohammad Shahriar Alam, Deputy Commissioner of the DMP's Protection Division, told Prothom Alo that reducing the number of ministerial escorts would lower fuel consumption while easing pressure on police vehicles and personnel.

He added that the vehicles and officers released from escort duties could now be deployed for routine policing across the capital.
