item.title: Trump faces midterm reckoning with 100 days to US vote
item.description:
One hundred days before the US midterm elections, President Donald Trump’s Republicans are staring down polling that points to the loss of the House of Representatives and a ferocious battle to retain the Senate.
Trump will not appear on the ballot on November 3, but the stakes for his presidency could hardly be higher.
A Democratic House would give the party control of powerful committees and subpoena authority, likely subjecting Trump’s administration to two years of investigations and potentially exposing him to a third impeachment drive.
Republicans enter the final stretch with a historically narrow House majority, weak presidential approval ratings, and an electorate increasingly unhappy about living costs and the grinding war with Iran.
US elections website Decision Desk HQ predicts that the Democratic Party has a 59% chance of winning the House, forecasting a 224-211 majority.
The president’s party usually loses ground in midterm elections, and only a handful of seats need to change hands.
Gasoline prices have climbed above $4 a gallon as the Iran war disrupts energy markets, inflation remains elevated, and interest rates are high.
Polling cited by Democrats suggests voters now trust them more than Republicans on inflation, health care, and even immigration, long considered a Republican strength.
“Donald Trump and Republicans have failed the American people,” House Democratic leader Hakeem Jeffries said Thursday, announcing an affordability campaign built around groceries, gasoline, housing, and health care.
Republicans insist the election will offer a choice between what Speaker Mike Johnson calls “common sense” and an increasingly progressive Democratic Party.
They plan to highlight border enforcement and tax cuts while portraying Democratic candidates as aligned with the socialist left.
Trump is pressing every available advantage.
He has waged a prolonged campaign for congressional Republicans to pass the SAVE America Act, which he portrays as essential to preventing election fraud but Democrats condemn as an attempt to suppress legitimate votes.
Republicans have been considerably more successful in another effort to shape the electorate: redrawing congressional maps.
Both parties have tried to carve out new safe seats, but Republicans look likely to emerge with a net advantage of between five and 12 seats.
That could offset the national political environment in a House contest expected to be decided by a similarly narrow margin.
Sarah Binder, a politics professor at George Washington University, said the redistricting arms race had been particularly consequential in this cycle, with fewer than one in 20 House races genuine toss-ups.
“Redistricting has really pared back the grounds on which Democrats can contest those seats,” she told AFP.
Republicans also hold a substantial financial advantage, with party campaign committees and allied groups entering the final months with tens of millions of dollars more than their Democratic counterparts.
The Senate presents a different but equally dramatic contest.
Republicans hold a 53-47 majority, meaning Democrats need a net gain of four seats. Decision Desk HQ narrowly favors Republicans to retain control through a 50-50 split, with Vice President JD Vance casting tie-breaking votes.
For Trump, even a divided Washington—with Democrats controlling the House and Republicans holding the Senate—would transform the remainder of his term.
His legislative agenda would stall in the House, his officials would face inquiries and public hearings, and Democrats would gain a national platform from which to scrutinize the Iran War, administration ethics, and the president’s attempts to reshape elections.
Political analyst Chuck Todd said in a podcast marking 100 days until the midterms that Republicans had gone from “clear favorites” in the Senate nine months ago to “very small favorites.”
House elections, he said, would likely yield a 10 to 25-seat Democratic advantage, pointing to Trump’s persistent low polling.
The president’s popularity remains near record lows in a new Economist/YouGov survey, with 36 percent of Americans saying they approve of his performance as president.
“There is no better predictor of a midterm than presidential job approval. A president’s job approval under 45 guarantees their party is going to lose seats. It doesn’t mean they’ll lose chambers, but they definitely lose seats,” the former news anchor said.
“A president under 40 -- they’re going to lose chambers. The question is, how bad is it? How big is the wave going to be?”

item.title: How CJP forced Modi’s second major retreat
item.description:
“Duniya jhukti hai, jhukanewala chahiye” -- the world bows, you just need someone to make it happen -- exulted Cockroach Janata Party (CJP) founder Abhijit Dipke soon after Dharmendra Pradhan resigned as education minister under pressure from the street agitation led by his outfit.
Ironically, the slogan, borrowed from a 1951 Bollywood film, was used by a Gen Z movement to celebrate its triumph in the standoff with the government of Prime Minister Narendra Modi.
Few could begrudge Dipke’s boast.
His outfit forced the Modi government to back down for only the second time in its 12-year tenure, the first being the repeal of the three controversial farm laws after months of sustained farmers’ protests in 2021.
What makes the CJP’s victory remarkable is its “winner-takes-all” outcome.
It succeeded in securing all three of its demands: Pradhan’s resignation, compensation for the families of those who died by suicide following the cancellation of the NEET examination, and the withdrawal of any FIRs against the protesters.
In fact, the joke in Delhi is that if the government ultimately had to concede all the CJP’s demands, why did it take so long, and what was the point of the rounds of negotiations held between July 20 and 25?
The CJP leadership repeatedly made it clear that Pradhan’s resignation was non-negotiable.
In the end, the government also accepted the other two demands.
While compensation for the affected families and the withdrawal of FIRs were relatively low-hanging fruit for the government, the real challenge was Pradhan’s removal.
He is widely regarded as one of the key architects of the BJP’s electoral strategy, making his ouster politically far more difficult.
What the farmers’ movement and the CJP agitation have in common is that both were driven directly by the affected stakeholders, with the legacy opposition parties playing only a supporting role, particularly in Parliament, where the CJP has no representation.
The significance of Pradhan’s resignation becomes clearer when viewed against the backdrop of what current Defence Minister Rajnath Singh once said during the controversy surrounding former IPL chairman Lalit Modi.
At the time, the Congress demanded the resignation of several senior BJP leaders for allegedly helping Lalit Modi leave the country.
Rajnath reportedly responded: “Ministers here do not resign. This is not the (Congress-led) UPA; this is the NDA.”
The UPA government, which ruled India from 2004 to 2014, witnessed the resignation of several senior ministers during its two terms, some over corruption allegations and others over alleged administrative failures.
Although leaders from several opposition parties joined Dipke and the student protesters at Jantar Mantar in central Delhi, the epicentre of the CJP movement, Congress leader Rahul Gandhi never visited the protest site.
Instead, he chose to stage a sit-in outside Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s residence in solidarity with the CJP.
To be fair, however, it must also be acknowledged that the opposition parties played a small but significant role in increasing pressure on the government by disrupting the first full week of the monsoon session of Parliament in solidarity with the protesters.
It is a common strategy for governments to hold their ground in the face of public protests, delaying concessions until the political cost of resistance becomes too high.
A former communications strategist for Arvind Kejriwal’s Aam Aadmi Party, Dipke’s greatest challenge was to prove that his massive online following could be converted into real-world mobilisation.
His campaign received a major boost from several prominent social activists, including Sonam Wangchuk.
Born out of a meme in May this year following Chief Justice of India Surya Kant’s reportedly controversial remarks, the CJP managed to achieve within just a couple of months what the opposition parties had failed to accomplish over the previous 12 years.
The chief justice later clarified that his remarks had been misquoted and were never intended as criticism of unemployed youth in general.
He said he was referring specifically to people entering professions with fake or bogus degrees, adding that reports claiming he had insulted young people were “totally baseless.”
On May 16, Dipke formally launched the Cockroach Janata Party as a satirical political movement. He also unveiled a website carrying the tagline, “Voice of the Lazy & Unemployed.”
Dipke described it as a platform for “all the ‘cockroaches’ out there,” with the tongue-in-cheek eligibility criteria including being unemployed, lazy, chronically online, and capable of ranting professionally.
The CJP gathered momentum as public anger intensified over the NEET-UG paper leak.
Dipke returned to India from the United States, where he had earned a master’s degree in public relations, in early June to personally lead the protests near Jantar Mantar.
Just before the protest was called off on July 25, Dipke had one final message for Chief Justice Surya Kant: “I thank CJI Kant for calling us cockroaches. Had you not called us cockroaches, Pradhan would not have resigned.”

item.title: PM: Govt committed to building modern, technology-driven army
item.description:
Prime Minister Tarique Rahman on Sunday said his government is committed to building a modern and technology-driven Bangladesh Army capable of meeting the demands of the time.
He said: "Bangladesh is currently facing complex and multidimensional security challenges, including maritime and border security, transnational and cross-border threats, cyber and information security, disaster response, and humanitarian assistance.
"As a result, it is now the demand of time to follow a realistic and sustainable model of defence modernisation, taking into account Bangladesh's geographical location, economic capacity, national security needs, and the expectations and tolerance of the people," he added.
The prime minister made the remarks while addressing the inaugural ceremony of the Army Headquarters Selection Board-2026 at the Dhaka Cantonment here this morning.
He said: "As prime minister and defence minister, I believe the strength of Bangladesh's defence lies not only in the capability of the armed forces but also in the unity, preparedness, and resilience of the entire nation".
Tarique Rahman said following the vision of Shaheed President Ziaur Rahman, the present government will formulate a modern policy under which the armed forces, law enforcement agencies, civil administration, industry, technology, educational institutions, and the country's people will work together as part of an integrated national security framework.
"The objective of this policy is not to promote war, but to build a well-prepared, stable, and self-reliant armed force capable of responding to any potential crisis, aggression, or disaster while safeguarding the country's sovereignty, independence, and national interests," he added.
Addressing senior army officials, the prime minister said that the nature of warfare has changed significantly.
"Security today is no longer limited to protecting territorial borders. It also encompasses cyberspace, information warfare, drone technology, artificial intelligence, and regional geopolitical competition," he said.
The premier said, therefore, the government wants to further strengthen the defence system by enhancing drone technology, satellite surveillance, and cyber and electronic warfare capabilities.
Tarique Rahman said the government is preparing a roadmap for the modernisation and development of the armed forces.
"Our vision for future force development prioritises capability over numbers, effectiveness alongside expansion, technological innovation over platform acquisition, and jointness rather than single force-centric development," he said.
The prime minister said the government's key priorities for strengthening the armed forces include building a disciplined, modern, and capable military, enhancing integrated defence planning, formulating time-befitting defence policies and strategies, promoting the domestic defence industry, and reinforcing democratic civil-military relations.
About the Army Headquarters Selection Board 2026, the prime minister said discipline in recruitment and promotion in the Bangladesh Army will be re-established through this Selection Board, which has been formed to duly identify and recognise qualified individuals based on merit, competence, efficiency, and integrity.
“At the same time, I believe it will establish a strong foundation for visionary and professional leadership in the Army of the future," he said, adding: “I feel a sense of pride in every success of the Army. On the other hand, I feel discomfort whenever there is any negative news concerning the Army.”
Noting that the cantonment is a place of deep emotion and memories for him, Tarique Rahman said: "As you know, my adolescent and youthful years were spent in a military environment, both at home and outside. Therefore, I am naturally quite familiar with the Army’s discipline, rules, and regulations. For these reasons, whenever I speak about the Army, I become somewhat nostalgic.”
He said: “I grew up with my parents, and my only younger brother within the disciplined and regulated environment followed in the Army. I always consider the Army as a part of my extended family.”
Recalling Shaheed President Ziaur Rahman, the proclaimer of the country’s independence, with due respect, Tarique Rahman said: “By declaring independence as an army officer, then Major Ziaur Rahman made the Army an inseparable part of the history of Bangladesh’s independence and Liberation War. Undoubtedly, this is a glorious chapter for the country’s Army.”
He said although the Army played a glorious role in the Liberation War, there were noticeable attempts immediately after independence to damage the Army’s image and create instability within it.
Prime Minister Tarique Rahman addresses the Army Headquarters Selection Board-2026 inaugural ceremony at Dhaka Cantonment on Sunday, July 26, 2026. Photo: PMO
Even during that turbulent period, under the firm and far-sighted leadership of former Army Chief, Shaheed Lieutenant General Ziaur Rahman, a new era of discipline and professionalism began in the Army, the prime minister said.
Since the very beginning of independence, members of the Army have been working tirelessly to maintain security and stability in the Chittagong Hill Tracts, he said, adding that the ongoing 1,036-kilometre-long Border Road project in the hill and border areas is not only ensuring border security but is also opening new opportunities for the livelihoods and economic activities of people living in remote areas.
In addition, the prime minister said that work is underway through the Army to clear mines and explosives from an area of 1,200 square metres in the hill region.
“I express my deepest condolences and gratitude to the families of the 217 brave Army personnel who embraced martyrdom while serving in peacekeeping and counter-terrorism operations in the Chittagong Hill Tracts,” he added.
The head of government said the reputation of the Bangladesh Army is now well established internationally, adding that by performing its duties with efficiency, professionalism, and dedication in United Nations peacekeeping missions, Bangladesh has earned special honor and prestige in the global arena over the past years as the highest troop-contributing country.
Tarique Rahman said: “Recently, members of the Bangladesh Army have performed their duties with great efficiency and professionalism in the Central African Republic, South Sudan, and Mali, thereby upholding the country’s honor in the international arena. Behind this glorious achievement lies a history of sacrifice.”
On December 13, 2025, six peacekeepers of the Bangladesh Army were martyred in a drone attack in South Sudan, he said, adding: “I pray for the forgiveness of the souls of the martyrs and express my deepest condolences to their bereaved families.”
About the Army’s role during the 2024 July Uprising, Tarique Rahman said: “I believe that the democracy-loving people will positively evaluate the responsible role played by the Army during the historic Student-People Mass Uprising of 2024 and in the critical moments following August 5.”
At the same time, throughout the tenure of the interim government, the Army played a commendable role in maintaining law and order, ensuring the security of industrial areas, and keeping the wheels of the stagnant economy moving, he added.
He said the Army’s wholehearted support in conducting the free and fair election held on February 12 was essentially a unique expression of its deep institutional commitment to democratic rules and regulations.
In addition, the prime minister said that even amid the global fuel oil crisis, the Army played a highly important role in maintaining normalcy by carrying out its responsibilities at oil storage facilities with efficiency and prudence.
He noted that the Bangladesh Army’s role in protecting the country’s sovereignty, combating terrorism in the Chittagong Hill Tracts, and serving in United Nations peacekeeping missions is highly commendable.
The Army has always played a leading role in the country’s infrastructure development, post-disaster rescue operations, and in responding to any national crisis, including the July Mass Uprising and flood situations, the premier said.
He further said: “During the fascist regime, every institution in the country lost its professionalism. The Army also had to face undesirable adverse circumstances. In the current democratic environment, the military must once again maintain the trust of the people by demonstrating its competence, skills, and professionalism.”
Regarding promotions in the Army, the prime minister said: “If certain specific policies are followed in promotions and appointments, the Army Headquarters Selection Board can play a groundbreaking role in establishing professionalism. Let merit and competence become the main criteria for an Army officer’s promotion.”
He said: “An officer’s physical fitness and physical appearance should be among the key considerations for promotion.”
Referring to the issue of physical fitness and regular exercise, the prime minister said he found a remark by the late US General Norman Schwarzkopf particularly relevant.
He said: "General H Norman Schwarzkopf said, ‘The more you sweat in peace, the less you bleed in war.’ Therefore, there is no room for compromise at any level regarding discipline and fitness in the Army.”
The prime minister hoped that the officers selected through the Selection Board would further strengthen the continuity of the Bangladesh Army’s success, glory, and professionalism in the future.
“The vision of the current government is ‘Bangladesh First’ in protecting the country’s interests. In protecting the interests of the people, it is ‘Bangladesh for All’,” he said.

item.title: Home minister stresses reward, punishment policy in police
item.description:
Home Minister Salahuddin Ahmed on Sunday reaffirmed the government's commitment to enforcing a strict reward and punishment policy to transform the country's law enforcement agencies into people-friendly and service-oriented institutions in line with the aspirations of the people following the July Mass Uprising.
"The reward and punishment policy will continue. Police personnel who perform their duties with honesty, courage and patriotism will receive due recognition and rewards, while those who violate laws and regulations, obstruct public service or engage in misconduct will face strict administrative and legal action," he said.
He made the remarks while addressing a ceremony as the chief guest at the Home Ministry's conference room, where certificates of recognition and financial rewards were presented to police personnel for acts of bravery and outstanding service.
Following the award ceremony, Ahmed briefed reporters on several contemporary and political issues.
Responding to a question about the improvised explosive device (IED) recovered beneath Motijheel Metro Rail Station, he said there was no basis to believe the device was planted to target the reverse Rath Yatra or any particular religious festival, describing the timing as coincidental.
He said the DMP Bomb Disposal Unit successfully neutralised the device and an investigation is underway.
On the resignation and security arrangements of former president Mohammed Shahabuddin, the minister said the resignation letter had been submitted to the speaker in accordance with the relevant constitutional provisions and had been accepted.
He said every citizen and political party has the right to express opinions and stage protests following the Mass Uprising.
He added that the constitutional immunity enjoyed by a former president for actions taken during tenure would remain in force.
Ahmed also said the former president is receiving full security through a coordinated arrangement involving the Special Security Force (SSF), the President's Guard Regiment (PGR) and the police.
Responding to questions over the absence of a police medal ceremony during this year's Police Week, the minister said technical errors and irregularities had been detected in the preliminary list prepared in haste.
The list is being re-examined, and medals will be awarded to deserving officers after completion of the verification process, he said.
Speaking at the event, Acting Secretary of the Home Ministry and Additional Secretary (Political and Immigration) Dr Ziauddin Ahmed delivered the welcome address.
Inspector General of Police (IGP) Md Ali Hossain Fakir, Dhaka Metropolitan Police (DMP) Commissioner Mosleh Uddin Ahmed, senior officials of the Home Ministry and Bangladesh Police were present.
DIG (Confidential) at Police Headquarters Md Kamrul Ahsan conducted the program.
A total of nine police personnel received awards for two separate acts of bravery and commendable service.
Seven police personnel were honoured for recovering a migrant worker's lost passport and other important documents within 30 minutes through the joint efforts of the National Emergency Service 999 and Dhaka Railway Police Station.
The recipients were Inspector (Unarmed) Zainal Abedin, ASIs (Unarmed) Mohammad Humayun Kabir and Md Rajikul Islam, Constables Md Shahinur Islam and Azmir Hossain of Dhaka Railway Police Station, and SI (Unarmed) Md Mizanur Rahman and Constable Bulbul Ahmed of National Emergency Service 999.
Two traffic sergeants—MS Mahmud Ali and Md Tuhinur Rahman Tuhin of the DMP Traffic Mirpur Division's Pallabi Zone—were also honoured for arresting a snatcher.

item.title: Death toll reaches 43 as 3 more die of dengue in 24 hrs
item.description:
Three people died of dengue and 458 new patients were admitted to hospitals across the country in 24 hours until 8:00am on Sunday.
With the latest fatalities, the dengue death toll has risen to 43 in the country this year, according to the Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS).
The new deaths were reported in Dhaka South City Corporation, Khulna and Barisal divisions, it said.
During the reporting period, 458 patients were discharged from hospitals after recovery.
Since January 1, a total of 13,098 dengue patients have been admitted to hospitals across the country.
Of them, 11,937 have recovered and been discharged, while 1,118 patients are currently undergoing treatment.

item.title: Jamuna erosion keeps Tangail regional road cut off for 6th day
item.description:
Traffic on the Tangail–Bhuapur–Tarakandi regional road remained suspended for the sixth consecutive day yesterday as repair work on a section washed away by erosion from the Jamuna River continued, causing widespread disruption and raising fears of further collapse.
The erosion began suddenly last Sunday at Sakharia village in Gopalpur upazila, where strong currents from the Jamuna River swept away an initial 25-metre stretch of the road. The damaged section has since widened to about 80 metres.
The road closure has halted the movement of passenger buses, freight vehicles and ambulances, forcing commuters and transport operators to use longer alternative routes. The detours have increased travel time, transportation costs and hardship for residents.
People living near the affected area have begun moving household belongings and livestock to safer locations amid concerns that further erosion could breach the remaining road and allow river water to inundate nearby settlements.
Officials from the Bangladesh Water Development Board (BWDB) are carrying out emergency protection work by dumping geo bags and tube bags along the eroding riverbank in an effort to stabilise the area.
Locals said they remain anxious despite the ongoing work, warning that failure to contain the erosion quickly could lead to extensive damage to homes, agricultural land and critical infrastructure.
"We are living in constant fear," said local resident Nazrul Islam. "If the road collapses completely, vast areas of Gopalpur, Bhuapur and the greater Mymensingh region could be affected."
Another resident, Md Hayrat, said villagers have been unable to sleep peacefully due to fears that the erosion could destroy their homes and farmland.
A resident named Anowara said her family had already moved their cattle to safer ground and feared they would have nowhere to go if the road gave way completely.
BWDB Executive Engineer Main Uddin attributed the erosion to heavy rainfall, strong upstream flows and changes in the Jamuna's channel caused by the formation of sandbars, which redirected the river's current towards the road.
"The affected section remains vulnerable. Geo bag dumping operations are continuing and will remain in place until the situation is brought under control," he said.
Local lawmaker Abdus Salam Pintu said emergency erosion-control measures were launched immediately after the collapse and that the government, BWDB and local residents were working together to prevent further damage.
The state minister for fisheries and livestock said more than 25,000 geo bags, along with large pipe bags, had already been deployed to reinforce the riverbank. He added that the government was also pursuing plans for a permanent embankment and hoped the emergency repair work would be completed soon.

item.title: Dev projects in Dumuria face uncertainty amid funding crisis
item.description:
Development projects worth around Tk1.70 crore in Dumuria Upazila of Khulna are facing uncertainty as the upazila administration’s development fund has almost run out of money.
The fund crisis has put several projects, including rural road construction, tube wells, religious institutions, educational facilities and other public infrastructure works, at risk of cancellation.
According to the upazila administration records, the development fund had a balance of Tk7.15 crore on 30 July 2025, while the revenue fund stood at Tk35 lakh .
However, at a meeting held on 21 May this year, officials said the balance in the development fund had dropped to only Tk3,729, while the revenue fund had increased to Tk3.30 core.
The figures show that nearly Tk7.15 crore was spent from the development fund within ten months, raising questions among local stakeholders over the utilisation of the money.
Meanwhile, the Upazila Engineering Department’s development projects worth Tk1.70 crore for the 2025–26 fiscal year are now at risk of being stalled due to the shortage of funds.
Contractors have already stopped 54 projects under seven packages, involving around Tk 80 lakh, after failing to receive work orders despite winning tenders through a lottery process held on 21 May.
Some contractors said they had completed assigned works and submitted bills, but later found that there was no money available in the development fund for payment.
The affected projects include road development, tube wells, mosques, temples, madrasas, educational institutions and paving works. Projects worth another Tk90 lakh are still at the tender invitation stage.
Sheikh Shahinur Rahman, president of the Dumuria Upazila Contractor Welfare Association, said contractors had suffered financial losses after spending money to participate in the tender process.
“More than 100 contractors submitted bids for projects under the Upazila Engineering Department. Each contractor spent around Tk7,500 on the tender process. Many won projects through the lottery, but work orders have not been issued,” he said.
He added that a meeting between contractors and the Upazila Executive Officer was held, but no solution had been found.
Dumuria Upazila Engineer Muhammad Darul Huda said the tender process was completed following government regulations, including newspaper advertisements and a lottery system.
“Work orders cannot be issued because there is no money available in the upazila development fund,” he said.
Upazila Executive Officer Sabita Sarkar said issuing work orders without sufficient funds would create further complications.
“If contractors are given work orders, they will complete the projects and submit bills. But there is no money in the fund to pay them,” she said.
Md Kamrul Islam Sardar, executive engineer of the Local Government Engineering Department (LGED), Khulna, said several projects under the 2025–26 fiscal year had been affected due to the fund shortage.
“If work orders are issued without available funds, contractors will complete the work and later face difficulties getting their payments,” he said.
The shortage of funds has raised concerns that important development activities in Dumuria may remain stalled unless additional financial support is arranged.

item.title: Govt primary school enrolment falls in Rajshahi
item.description:
Enrolment in government primary schools across Rajshahi division has declined over the past 12 years despite population growth, while private kindergartens and madrasas have continued to attract more students, according to official data.
Figures from the Divisional Deputy Director's Office of Primary Education show that student enrolment in government primary schools dropped from 1,320,975 in 2014 to 1,183,992 in 2026, a decline of 136,983. During the same period, the population of Rajshahi division increased by around 2.5 million.
In contrast, enrolment in private primary schools, including kindergartens, rose from 436,966 to 504,030 students. Officials also said admissions to Alia and Qawmi madrasas have increased steadily, although consolidated enrolment data were unavailable.
Educationists say the shift reflects growing concerns among parents about the quality of education in government schools, as well as stronger confidence in private institutions.
Head teachers across the division said the rapid expansion of kindergartens and madrasas has contributed significantly to declining enrolment in government schools.
Afroza Khatun, head teacher of Kantanagar Government Primary School in Bagmara upazila, said the school's enrolment had fallen from around 100 students to about 60 after two kindergartens opened nearby.
At Atkoshi Government Primary School in Rajshahi city, enrolment has dropped from more than 550 students five years ago to around 350, according to head teacher Nilufa Akhtar Khanam.
"There are at least 10 kindergarten schools and several madrasas within one kilometre of our school. Many students have transferred there," she said.
Teachers from more than two dozen government primary schools interviewed by this correspondent reported similar trends, with many citing increased admissions to nearby kindergartens and madrasas.
Nikhil Ranjan Pramanik, a teacher at Kachua-2 Government Primary School in Tanore upazila, said 17 students recently left his school to enrol in a nearby madrasa.
"We are trying to improve the quality of education, but admissions continue to decline every year," he said.
Parents said they preferred kindergartens because of regular assessments, closer teacher supervision, better communication with families and greater emphasis on English-language education.
"Government schools are free, but we are not satisfied with the quality of education," said Mustafizur Rahman, a parent in Rajshahi city. "Kindergarten teachers closely monitor children and regularly update parents on their progress."
Another guardian, Saju, whose son attends Shaheen School in Rajshahi, said he chose a private school because he believed it offered better-quality education and stronger English instruction.
Domestic worker Asma Begum said she enrolled her daughter in a kindergarten despite financial hardship because she wanted her to receive a better education.
Professor Dr Akhter Banu, director of the Institute of Education and Research at Rajshahi University, said parents ultimately choose schools they trust.
"Even many government primary school teachers prefer to enrol their own children in private schools instead of the schools where they teach. That reflects declining confidence in the public education system," she said.
She said weak supervision, limited teacher motivation and a lack of accountability have undermined public trust, while private schools maintain closer communication with parents.
"Unless supervision, accountability and teacher motivation improve, parents will continue to shift their children to other institutions," she added.
Nur Akhtar Jannatul Ferdous, assistant director at the Rajshahi Divisional Deputy Director's Office of Primary Education, said more research was needed to determine the reasons behind the decline in enrolment.
"It is not possible to identify a single reason at this stage. A detailed study is needed to understand the factors involved," she said.

item.title: Tangail bridge approach damaged by heavy rainfall
item.description:
Heavy rainfall has damaged a section of the approach to a bridge by the Local Government Engineering Department (LGED) at Shyamar Ghat on the Tangail–Hugra road in Tangail Sadar upazila, making vehicular movement risky.
On Sunday afternoon, LGED Executive Engineer Jahanara Parvin, who recently joined the district, inspected the damaged bridge approach and said repairs would be carried out soon.
According to residents, a section of the bridge approach collapsed during the current monsoon season due to heavy rainfall, creating risks for vehicles crossing the bridge.
The bridge is used daily by thousands of people from Hugra, Dyenna, Katuli and Kakua in the char areas of Tangail Sadar upazila, as well as Chauhali in Sirajganj district. Residents said the same section of the approach had collapsed several times in the past and called for a permanent solution.
After being informed about the damage, Jahanara Parvin visited the site and inspected the affected area.
She said: “The bridge approach was damaged due to heavy rainfall. After the inspection, the matter has been reported to the higher authorities. We hope the repairs will be completed quickly so that the bridge becomes suitable for vehicular movement.”
LGED Sub-Assistant Engineer Mostafizur Rahman and other department officials were present during the inspection.
The bridge was constructed around 15 years ago to improve transportation for residents of the surrounding char areas.

item.title: HC sets Aug 2 for verdict on Chinmoy’s bail in 2 cases
item.description:
The High Court on Sunday set August 2 to deliver the verdict on the rule over the bail of Bangladesh Sammilito Sanatani Jagaran Jote spokesperson Chinmoy Krishna Das Brahmachari, also known as Chandan Kumar Dhar, in two cases.
A High Court bench comprising Justice KM Zahid Sarwar Kajol and Justice Sheikh Abu Taher set August 2 for delivering the verdict after concluding the hearing on the rule.
Advocate Apurba Kumar Bhattacharya appeared for Chinmoy Das during the hearing.
Earlier, the High Court had issued a rule asking why Chinmoy Das should not be granted bail in the two vandalism cases.
On October 31, 2024, Firoz Khan, general secretary of the BNP's Mohra Ward unit in Chittagong, filed a sedition case with Kotwali Police Station against Chinmoy Krishna Das and 18 others. Chinmoy Das and several co-accused were subsequently arrested in the case.
Separately, clashes erupted on the Chittagong court premises on November 26, 2025, after a court denied Chinmoy Das bail in the sedition case, allegedly following unrest by his supporters.
During the violence, lawyer Saiful Islam was beaten and hacked to death. Nearly two dozen suspects have since been arrested over the killing, while additional cases were later filed against Chinmoy Das.

item.title: Marvel announces ‘Black Panther III’ at Comic-Con
item.description:
Superhero movie fans will officially return to the world of Wakanda in “Black Panther III,” the newest entry in the Marvel film franchise, the studio announced at Comic-Con on Saturday.
British actor David Jonsson will play the lead role in the film, due out on December 15, 2028.
Known for his performances in the HBO television series “Industry” and the 2025 film “The Long Walk,” Jonsson steps into the Marvel Cinematic Universe as the son of T’Challa, the original Black Panther superhero played by actor Chadwick Boseman.
Boseman, who rocketed to fame in 2018’s “Black Panther,” died in 2020 at the age of 43 as a result of colon cancer.
Marvel announced the Black Panther threequel with Jonsson appearing in front of thousands of fans at Comic-Con’s famous Hall H.
“Thank you to this amazing family that I have the honor and the privilege and the blessing to join,” Jonsson told the crowd.
“I actually don’t want to say too much because I want to let this screen do the talk,” he said.
Oscar-winning filmmaker Ryan Coogler, who directed the first two “Black Panther” films, will return to helm the third.
“Today is extra special,” Coogler said, joining Jonsson and Marvel executive producer Kevin Feige on stage.
Coogler told the audience “Black Panther III” will follow T’Challa’s son as he comes of age and follows in his father’s superhero-sized footsteps.
The first “Black Panther” film grossed $1.3 billion when it was released in 2018, starring Boseman alongside a cast including Michael B. Jordan—who won this year’s Best Actor Oscar—Angela Bassett, Lupita Nyong’o, Forest Whitaker, Danai Gurira, and Letitia Wright, many of whom reprised their appearances in “Black Panther 2.”
Another bombshell reveal was the welcome of Ryan Gosling to the Marvel Cinematic Universe, where he will take on the role of Johnny Blaze in “Ghost Rider,” slated to hit theaters in 2028.
“Is this really happening?” Gosling said onstage alongside Feige.
Marvel Studios returned to Hall H after skipping last year’s event, less than five months before the release of its highly anticipated “Avengers: Doomsday.”
The studio brought to the stage Anthony and Joe Russo, the directors of the film, as well as several of its stars, including Robert Downey Jr., who will play the villain Victor Von Doom.
The latest superhero film will pick up where 2019’s “Endgame” left off, bringing together heroes and villains from the X-Men, the Avengers, Black Panther, and the Fantastic Four to duke it out once more.
Capes and masks of the nefarious Victor von Doom were handed out before Marvel’s presentation, transforming the audience into a green army.
Some fans had waited several nights to get into the venue to hear from their favorite studio.
“We’re all here for the same reason; we love it, we love the feeling we get when we come to Hall H,” Wally, a man from neighboring Orange County who slept outside the venue for two nights, told AFP.
“It was worth it; it was better than expected... I’m speechless,” he said after the presentation.
Earlier in the day, Apple TV made its debut in the coveted Hall H, offering a first look at its upcoming action comedy “Matchbox: The Movie.”
The streaming platform unveiled some footage from the flick, which stars John Cena, Jessica Biel, Sam Richardson, Teyonah Parris, and Arturo Castro.
The film is inspired by the famous toy cars, which Biel said she grew up playing with her brother.
“It’s like being a kid again,” she said.
Apple TV also offered an early look at its science-fiction production “Neuromancer,” based on William Gibson’s 1984 novel, and “Mayday,” a comedy set during the Cold War starring Ryan Reynolds and Kenneth Branagh.
Comic-Con runs through Sunday, July 26.

item.title: Complaints lodged with ICT against former presidents Hamid, Shahabuddin
item.description:
Complaints have been lodged with the Office of the Chief Prosecutor of the International Crimes Tribunal (ICT) against former President Mohammed Shahabuddin, who recently resigned from office.

The complaints were submitted separately on Sunday by two organisations—Bangladesh Azadi Party and the Rashtra Sanglap Forum. The Azadi Party also filed a complaint against former President M Abdul Hamid.

Following the submissions, Lieutenant Colonel (retd) Md Hasinur Rahman, Convener of the Azadi Party, spoke to journalists.

He alleged that the two former presidents had remained silent while so many people were killed and forcibly disappeared up to 5 August. He claimed that their silence amounted to tacit approval of those alleged crimes.

The party's Chief Organiser, Munshi Borhan Mahmud, said the complaints concerned former presidents Abdul Hamid and Mohammed Shahabuddin.

He alleged that, during their respective tenures as Head of State, Bangladesh witnessed incidents including the Pilkhana carnage, the Shapla crackdown, judicial killings, enforced disappearances, murders, the “Aynaghar” (a secret detention facility) detention facilities, and other alleged mass atrocities.

He further claimed that the two former presidents had supported the then government, provided it with political legitimacy, failed to protest against those alleged abuses, and benefited from remaining part of the state establishment.

Munshi Borhan Mahmud also argued that they could not evade responsibility for those events.

Rashtra Sanglap Forum’s complaint

The Rashtra Sanglap Forum filed a separate complaint naming only former President Mohammed Shahabuddin.

In the complaint submitted to the chief prosecutor’s office, the organisation’s Central Member Secretary, Al Noor Mohammad Ayas, alleged that he had been forcibly disappeared from Mohakhali Bus Terminal in Dhaka on the night of 18 January last year while travelling to Mymensingh after leading demonstrations in Shahbagh demanding Shahabuddin's resignation.

He claimed that he was abandoned in the Banglamotor area the following day.

The complaint also described Shahabuddin as a “close associate” of ousted Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina. It called for an investigation into Shahabuddin's alleged role as an instigator of the shooting of student protesters and civilians during the July mass uprising, as well as torture, killings and enforced disappearances.

In addition, the complaint urged an independent and impartial investigation to determine whether Shahabuddin bore any legal responsibility or involvement in relation to the 2024 general election, human rights violations, and events connected with the July uprising.

Asked about the complaints during a media briefing, Chief Prosecutor Md Aminul Islam declined to comment on the matter.

item.title: Pedestrian killed as bus ploughs into Kurmitola Hospital compound
item.description:
A pedestrian was killed and two others, including a child, were injured after a passenger bus veered out of control and ploughed into the compound of Kurmitola General Hospital in the capital on Sunday night.
The deceased, Rafiqul Islam, was an employee of a local hotel.
Deputy Commissioner of Police (Gulshan Division) Tanvir Hasan confirmed the incident.
According to police and local sources, the driver of a Poristhan Paribahan bus lost control while attempting to pull over in the Kurmitola area to drop off passengers.
The bus veered into the compound of Kurmitola General Hospital, crashing through part of the wall of a gas control room beside the main gate. Rafiqul Islam, who was standing near the entrance, was struck by the bus and died on the spot.
Police from Cantonment Police Station later detained the bus driver in connection with the incident.

item.title: Jamaat calls for urgent action to ease gas crisis
item.description:
Bangladesh Jamaat-e-Islami on Sunday urged the government and relevant authorities to take immediate and effective measures to resolve the ongoing gas crisis and provide relief to people suffering from the shortage.
In a statement, the party's Assistant Secretary General Advocate Zubair said people across the country are facing an acute shortage of LPG and CNG gas, which are essential commodities.
He expressed deep concern over widespread disruptions to daily cooking, CNG-powered transport services and industrial production due to the crisis.
He also said long queues of vehicles have been seen at CNG stations in the capital because of the severe gas shortage.
"As a result, millions of working hours of citizens are being wasted, and public suffering has reached its peak. People believe that illegal gas connections, government mismanagement, irregularities and syndicates are largely responsible for the crisis," he said.
He demanded an investigation into whether any group was attempting to create an artificial gas shortage to increase prices and urged authorities to take effective measures to reduce public suffering.
Zubair also called for exploring and drilling new gas wells, ensuring extraction from existing wells and securing necessary LNG imports in line with public demand.
He alleged that the government is focused on securing the interests of unscrupulous groups rather than addressing citizens' basic needs, resulting in a severe gas crisis across the country.

item.title: Educational institutions to observe 21 holidays in August, September
item.description:
Teachers and students at educational institutions across the country will observe a total of 21 holidays in August and September, including weekly holidays, according to the academic calendar.
The calendar shows that August will have 9 weekly holidays. In addition, educational institutions will remain closed on August 5 for July Mass Uprising Day, August 12 for Akheri Chahar Somba, and August 26 for Eid-e-Miladunnabi.
In total, educational institutions will observe 12 holidays in August.
September will have 8 weekly holidays. Educational institutions will also remain closed on September 24 for Fateha-i-Yazdaham.
Madhu Purnima and Mahalaya fall on Saturdays and therefore will not be counted as additional holidays.
As a result, educational institutions will observe 9 holidays in September, bringing the combined total for August and September to 21.

item.title: Four bodies recovered in Naogaon within six hours
item.description:
Police recovered the bodies of four people from different parts of Naogaon within a span of six hours on Sunday.
Three of them died after drowning, while the body of another youth was recovered from his home.
In Badalgachhi upazila, Nur Islam, and Sumaiya Akter, drowned in a canal near Kartikahar village while bathing around noon. Locals rescued them and took them to Badalgachhi Upazila Health Complex, where doctors declared them dead.
Nur was from Gangni upazila of Meherpur, while Sumaiya was the daughter of Shahin Hossain of Kartikahar village.
Badalgachhi Police Station Officer-in-Charge (OC) Muhammad Ruhul Amin said the bodies were handed over to the families without autopsies following their applications.
In Raninagar, farmer Abdul Mondal, drowned after falling from a boat in a waterbody in Belbari village while returning home after cutting grass for cattle. His body was recovered after about three and a half hours of search by locals and a Fire Service diving team.
Raninagar Police Station OC Md Zakaria Mondal said the body was handed over to the family without an autopsy following their request.
Meanwhile, police recovered the body of Limon Hasan, from his room in Bandhaikhara Sardarpara area of Atrai upazila in the morning.
Police said Limon’s family found him dead after breaking open the door when he did not respond in the morning. His body was sent to Naogaon Sadar Hospital morgue for autopsy.
Atrai Police Station OC Mahbub Alam said police recovered the body and sent it to Naogaon Sadar Hospital morgue for autopsy.
“An unnatural death case has been filed and the incident is being investigated,” he said.

item.title: 'Use Nazrul Barsho logo on official letters until May 2027'
item.description:
The Cabinet Division has directed all government offices to use the designated logo of ‘Nazrul Barsho’ in official letters until May 25, 2027.
A letter containing the instruction was sent on Sunday to the senior secretaries and secretaries of all ministries and divisions, divisional commissioners, deputy commissioners (DCs) and all Upazila Nirbahi Officers (UNOs).
The letter said the government has declared the period from May 25, 2026 to May 25, 2027 as ‘Nazrul Barsho’.
On the occasion, the Prime Minister unveiled the designated logo of ‘Nazrul Barsho’ on July 2.
It further said that, as part of efforts to uphold the ideals, spirit and literary works of national poet Kazi Nazrul Islam in the thoughts and actions of the nation and to observe ‘Nazrul Barsho’ with due dignity, the Ministry of Cultural Affairs requested the use of the designated logo on all official letters until May 25, 2027.

item.title: IUB book discussion explores how grandmothers keep family stories alive
item.description:
The anthology "Stories My Grandma (Never) Told Me" transforms the oral histories women have long shared in kitchens and family gatherings into a lasting literary record, academics and writers said at a book discussion hosted by Independent University, Bangladesh (IUB) on Sunday.
The book edited by Professor Razia Sultana Khan of IUB was discussed at an event organised by the Department of English and Modern Languages at the DMK Lecture Gallery of IUB.
Speaking as a discussant, Professor Firdous Azim of BRAC University said the anthology carried personal resonance for her as a grandmother herself.
She said her six-year-old granddaughter sleeps beside her every night waiting to hear stories, an experience that revived her own memories of tales told by her grandmothers.
Reading and writing in English, she said, allows such stories to be passed on to students and offers them a wider perspective on family and history.
Iftekhar Ahmed Chowdhury, president of the Cosmos Foundation and former Foreign Affairs Adviser, described the book as a tribute that turns the "whispers of resilience" and unspoken truths of women into a powerful "chorus," arguing that domestic spaces such as kitchens and funerals are where history is truly forged.
Calling the volume a "vibrant tapestry," he said while the book celebrates oral history, the figure of the grandmother often serves as a metaphor through which the authors channel their own contemporary reflections.
He recommended the book not merely as a record of the past but as a portrait of the writers themselves, saying the grandmothers in its pages, real or imagined, remain the "keepers of us."
Sayyeda Tun Noor Sameera, a faculty member at IUB, called the anthology a beautifully produced and accessible volume, noting that an English-language book of this kind published in Bangladesh remains a rare occurrence.
She said editor Razia had brought together the everyday stories grandmothers commonly tell their grandchildren, adding that such stories leave a lasting imprint on children's nostalgic memories and that the bond between grandmother and grandchild, built through storytelling, evokes something akin to seeking nirvana.
Elita Karim, musician and a PhD student at Arizona State University, reflected on the role women play in passing down knowledge and memory through stories, music and poetry, saying the anthology captures this tradition as an art form in its own right.
Following the discussion, editor Razia Sultana Khan introduced the contributing writers to the audience.
According to the book's flap copy, the stories in the anthology are written by members of The Reading Circle (TRC), a community of readers spanning continents, genres and cultures who have previously translated works by Kazi Nazrul Islam and Alice Munro and compiled personal narratives in "Stories from the Edge: Personal Narratives of 1971."
The new collection grew out of the group's fascination with the family secrets and hidden histories that persist across generations, resurfacing much like banned books circulated underground.

item.title: Nur: Govt working to resolve UAE visa issues
item.description:
The government is working to resolve visa-related issues affecting Bangladeshi workers seeking employment in the United Arab Emirates (UAE), State Minister for Expatriates' Welfare and Overseas Employment Nurul Haque Nur has said.
In a Facebook post on Sunday, the state minister said the government is aware of the ongoing visa issues and is engaging with the relevant authorities to find a solution.
"We are aware of the UAE visa complications. Discussions are underway with the concerned authorities to resolve the matter," he wrote, adding that the government remains committed to protecting the interests of its citizens.
"If we can do something positive for our expatriates, it will be good both for them and for the government," he said.
Nur acknowledged that the frustration among migrant workers is understandable, attributing it to years of mismanagement and neglect.
He said efforts have been underway since he assumed office to improve the situation.
"Let's see how much we can achieve. It may take time, but I hope we will be able to bring positive changes," he wrote.

item.title: Health minister visits Tala Health Complex, promises upgrade to 100-bed hospital
item.description:
Health and Family Welfare Minister Sardar Md Sakhawat Hossain made a surprise visit to Tala Upazila Health Complex in Satkhira on Sunday, inspecting hospital facilities and pledging to upgrade the facility to a 100-bed hospital.
Arriving at around 10:30 am, the minister began his inspection in the hospital kitchen, where he sampled food prepared for patients to assess its quality. He later toured the male and female wards, medicine store, operating theatre (OT), administrative offices, washrooms, and staff attendance registers.
During the visit, he met patients to hear their views on medical treatment, medicine availability, and the overall quality of healthcare services. He also inspected the hospital premises and discussed service challenges and future development plans with local residents and officials.
The minister instructed hospital authorities to improve healthcare services and ordered action against those responsible for the theft of air-conditioning units from the hospital. He also directed officials to expedite ongoing renovation work, including improvements to washroom facilities and called for administrative action against a medical officer who has reportedly remained absent from duty for an extended period.
Speaking to reporters after the visit, Hossain said the government is continuing to recruit doctors through a special Bangladesh Civil Service (BCS) process to address staffing shortages. He added that the recruitment process for 100,000 healthcare workers has also begun.
The minister announced that work to upgrade Tala Upazila Health Complex to a 100-bed facility will begin soon, with soil testing expected in the coming weeks.
He said the project includes constructing a modern seven-to- eight-storey building equipped with separate paralysis rehabilitation centers for men and women, a physiotherapy center, a breastfeeding corner, and a trauma center to strengthen healthcare services for the region.

item.title: ‘Media freedom must come with responsibility’
item.description:
The government is working on a new legal and policy framework to guarantee media freedom while tackling misinformation, Information and Broadcasting Minister Zahir Uddin Swapon has said, promising that journalists will face no government obstruction but warning that freedom cannot become a licence for disinformation or abuse.
In an exclusive interview with Dhaka Tribune, the BNP leader said the government is reviewing recommendations of the Media Reform Commission, drafting a comprehensive Right to Information law, strengthening its capacity to combat digital misinformation and studying international models from the UK, Australia and the European Union.
He also acknowledged the government’s responsibility for Bangladesh’s failure to build globally competitive media institutions and pledged to modernize state-owned broadcasters.
Zahir Uddin Swapon: Our government was elected through a democratic process, and Prime Minister Tarique Rahman has made it clear that responsible media freedom must be ensured. The government should never obstruct journalism, but freedom must not be abused to spread misinformation or create confusion. We are consulting all media stakeholders to establish that balance.
We are carefully reviewing all previous commission reports and recommendations. We are not rejecting any constructive proposal. Our goal is to develop an effective and broadly acceptable framework by combining past recommendations with present realities.
Investigative journalism is essential for accountability and democracy. At the same time, there have been instances where investigative reporting has been misused for blackmail. We want to encourage genuine investigative journalism while developing safeguards against abuse through consultation with media stakeholders. This issue is also part of the Media Commission’s discussions.
The interim government introduced an ordinance, but we do not consider it a permanent solution. Access to information is a fundamental right. We are working on a comprehensive and updated law after extensive consultations with stakeholders.
Our existing institutional structure was built for traditional media. Digital platforms require different skills and technologies. We have therefore launched a New Media project to build technical capacity and develop skilled professionals capable of identifying and countering disinformation.
The challenge has changed. Earlier, the priority was securing media freedom. Today, protecting people from disinformation is equally important. That requires cooperation between the government, professional journalists and global technology companies. We are studying regulatory models adopted by the UK, Australia and the European Union to develop policies suited to Bangladesh.
The problem has long been the absence of a national consensus on the limits and responsibilities of media freedom. We want to protect freedom of expression while preventing disorder and misinformation. Our approach is to build that framework through dialogue with all stakeholders rather than imposing unilateral decisions.
Although we now live in a digital ecosystem, much of our infrastructure remains analogue. Our first priority is digital transformation. Once that capacity is built, state-owned media can become more competitive through modern technology and content that appeals to younger audiences.
In my view, the greater problem has often been the application of the law rather than the law itself. Unless we clearly define what constitutes legitimate information, disinformation and criminal conduct, there will always be room for misuse. We want the legal framework to be transparent, precise and fairly enforced.
Certainly. Every government bears responsibility. We have only recently taken office, but we must learn from past failures. Having experienced undue pressure on the media and restrictions on the free flow of information while in opposition, we want to build an independent, responsible and internationally competitive media environment.

item.title: Bangladesh announce Test squad for historic Australia tour
item.description:
The Bangladesh Cricket Board (BCB) on Sunday has announced a 15-member squad for the first Test against Australia, with uncapped fast bowler Musfik Hasan earning a place in the side.
The tour marks Bangladesh's first Test series in Australia in 23 years. None of the players in the current squad has previously played a Test match on Australian soil.
A series of injuries to Bangladesh's pace attack, including the absence of speedster Nahid Rana, has left the selectors with limited options, paving the way for Musfik's inclusion.
Although Musfik is yet to make his Test debut, this is not his first call-up to the national squad. He was previously included for the one-off Test against Afghanistan in 2023 and the home series against Sri Lanka in 2024 but did not feature in either match.
Nahid Rana has been ruled out of the entire two-Test series due to injury. Left-arm pacer Shoriful Islam, however, is expected to return for the second Test, for which the squad is yet to be announced.
Taskin Ahmed, Hasan Mahmud, Ebadot Hossain, Syed Khaled Ahmed are the other four pacers to includ into the squad alongside Musfik.
Bangladesh have also been dealt a blow with wicketkeeper-batter Liton Das ruled out of the opening Test. He is, however, expected to recover in time for the second and final match of the series.
The Bangladesh team will depart for Australia on August 1 and will play a three-day warm-up match against a Cricket Australia XI at DXC Arena in Darwin from August 6 to 8.
The first Test will be held at Marrara Cricket Ground in Darwin from August 13, while the second and final Test is scheduled to begin on August 22 at Great Barrier Reef Arena in Mackay.
Squad for 1st Test: Najmul Hossain Shanto (Captain), Soumya Sarkar, Shadman Islam, Tanzid Hasan Tamim, Mominul Haque, Mushfiqur Rahim, Amite Hasan, Jaker Ali Anik, Mehidy Hasan Miraz (Vice Captain), Taijul Islam, Taskin Ahmed, Hasan Mahmud, Syed Khaled Ahmed, Ebadot Hossain Chowdhury, Musfik Hasan.

item.title: Walton expands global business network to Libya
item.description:
Bangladeshi tech giant Walton is expanding its reach in the international market with the vision of securing a place among the top global electronics brands.
To achieve this goal, the company is actively working to expand its brand business across 100 countries.
As part of this ongoing effort, Libya—a North African nation—has recently joined Walton’s global business network.
In pursuit of this expansion, an agreement was signed recently at the Walton corporate office in the capital between Libyan electronics marketing company Asr Al Teqnia and Walton Hi-Tech Industries PLC.
Under the contract, Asr Al Teqnia will act as the official distributor of Walton products in Libya, marketing and selling high-tech products including refrigerators, televisions, air conditioners, and washing machines.
The agreement was signed by Md Ziaul Alam, additional managing director and chief financial officer of Walton Hi-Tech, and Al Sadiq Al Tahir Al Saghir Karah, managing director of Asr Al Teqnia, on behalf of their respective organizations.
Abdur Rouf, chief of Walton Global Business Division, stated that Walton holds a competitive edge over other international brands due to its innovative technology, modern designs, durability, high quality, energy efficiency, eco-friendliness, and competitive pricing. As a result, the Walton brand rapidly gains consumer trust in global markets, leading to continuous expansion into new countries. Walton's brand presence has already spread across 55 countries, with Libya now becoming the newest addition to the list.
He further mentioned that two shipments of Walton-branded refrigerators, air conditioners, televisions, and washing machines have already been exported to Libya this year.
The company expects that expanding business operations in Libya will pave the way for smoother market entry into other North African nations.
The signing ceremony was also attended by Walton chief marketing officer Zoheb Ahmed, deputy head of Walton Global Business Division Sayeid Al Imran, and Libya country manager Abdul Latif Pramanik, among other senior-ranking officials.

item.title: PM visits UIU stall at Bear Summit & National Semiconductor Symposium 2026
item.description:
United International University (UIU) was honoured to welcome Prime Minister Tarique Rahman to its exhibition stall at the Bear (Biotechnology, Electronics, AI and Robotics) Summit & National Semiconductor Symposium 2026 at the Novo Theatre, Dhaka.
During his visit, the prime minister explored several of UIU's flagship innovations, including the UIU Mars Rover, UIU Rescue Rover, and UIU Mariner, as well as many groundbreaking research and commercialization initiatives.
The exhibition also showcased innovative projects such as SmartEndo, Bolte Chai, Smart Autism Barta, BScan, and Brain-Computer Interface (BCI) research, demonstrating UIU's growing contributions to research, innovation, technology commercialization, and societal development.
The prime minister expressed keen interest in the university's research and innovation initiatives.
His visit and appreciation served as a significant recognition of UIU's unwavering commitment to transforming research into impactful technologies and commercially viable solutions that address real-world challenges.

item.title: Al-Arafah Islami Bank holds agent banking views exchange meeting & Courtyard Gathering at Barisal
item.description:
To expand financial inclusion by delivering modern, secure and Shariah-compliant banking services to the doorsteps of underserved communities, Al-Arafah Islami Bank PLC organized an Agent Banking Views Exchange Meeting and Courtyard Meeting with the participation of owners of 82 agent outlets, managers of 10 link branches, outlet managers and selected customers from Barisal region.
The program, held on July 23, was attended by deputy managing director and head of the bank's agent banking & digital banking wing Md Aminul Islam Bhuiyan as chief guest.
Vice president and manager of Mathbaria branch Md Enayet Fakir and senior assistant vice president of the agent banking division Md Ishtiaq Hasan attended as special guests.
The meeting was presided over by manager of Barishal branch Muhammad Abdus Shukur.
During the daylong program, agent outlet owners, branch managers, outlet managers and selected customers shared their experiences and discussed various operational challenges, possible solutions, strategies for deposit growth and ways to ensure modern, secure and cashless banking services through the bank's digital channels, including Digital Danbox, Bangla QR, Islamic Wallet, Internet Banking, IlmNet – Education Management System, and the Digital Payment Collection Module.
Speaking on the occasion, Md Aminul Islam Bhuiyan said that Al-Arafah Islami Bank PLC is further strengthening its Agent Banking operations to deliver modern and Shariah-compliant banking services to the doorsteps of underserved communities across the country.
He urged agent outlet owners, branch managers and outlet managers to work in close coordination to accelerate deposit mobilization, enhance customer service and strengthen financial inclusion initiatives.
He also advised customers to complete transactions using fingerprint authentication at agent outlets, collect the system-generated transaction receipt and verify the SMS confirmation after each transaction.
He further encouraged customers to adopt the Bank's digital channels, including Bangla QR, Digital Danbox, Islamic Wallet, Internet Banking and IlmNet, to enjoy convenient and secure cashless banking services.
At the end of the meeting, the participants expressed their commitment to working together to further strengthen the bank's agent banking operations, expand access to modern and Shariah-compliant banking services for underserved communities, and support Bangladesh Bank's initiatives for greater financial inclusion and the expansion of cashless transactions.

item.title: Nestlé, BCSIR showcase pioneering innovation in nutrition solution at Ficci FDI Conference 2026
item.description:
Nestlé Bangladesh PLC showcased the outcome of its pioneering collaboration with the Bangladesh Council of Scientific and Industrial Research (BCSIR) at the Ficci FDI Conference 2026 – Driving Foreign Investment for Jobs and Prosperity in Bangladesh, held at the Bangladesh-China Friendship Conference Centre in Dhaka on July 23.
This partnership reflects a shared commitment to advancing nutrition and supporting Bangladesh’s long-term human capital development.
The collaboration resulted in Pushtigrow+, a locally developed cereal-based micronutrient fortifier for children aged five and above.
Co-created by Nestlé Bangladesh and BCSIR, it enriches daily home-cooked meals with probiotics, iron, zinc, and essential vitamins, helping improve everyday nutrition at scale.
Prime Minister Tarique Rahman, along with senior dignitaries visited the Nestlé Bangladesh pavilion and commended this innovative micronutrient solution.
Samina Ahmed, chairman, BCSIR, said: “By combining BCSIR’s scientific capabilities with Nestlé’s global nutrition expertise, we are strengthening Bangladesh’s innovation ecosystem. This collaboration shows how public-private partnerships can create lasting value for the nation.”
Commenting on this collaboration, Deepal Abeywickrema, chairman & managing director, Nestlé Bangladesh PLC, said: “Our collaboration with BCSIR reflects our commitment to addressing micronutrient deficiencies through affordable, everyday nutrition solutions.”

item.title: Sooryavanshi's 81 steers India to Zimbabwe T20 series sweep
item.description:
Teenage cricket sensation Vaibhav Sooryavanshi scored his second half century in four days for India, who beat Zimbabwe by 35 runs on Sunday for a 3-0 Twenty20 international series sweep.
India won the toss and posted 192-5 at Harare Sports Club, led by a quickfire 81 from Sooryavanshi. He faced 49 balls and his innings included four sixes and eight fours.
Zimbabwe, 10 places below second-placed India in the world T20I rankings, reached 157-7 in reply thanks mainly to an unbeaten 54 from lower-order batter Ryan Burl.
Victory marked an Indian turnaround after a 2-0 T20I series loss in Ireland, then a 4-0 drubbing in England. It was the second straight series loss for Zimbabwe after going down 2-1 to Bangladesh.
At 15, Sooryavanshi is the youngest cricketer to represent India. He has sparkled in southern Africa after debuting in the England series and amassing 42 runs over three innings.
Sooryavanshi has had a memorable tour of Zimbabwe. He scored his maiden T20I half-century off just 18 balls in the first match and followed it up with 20 off nine deliveries in the second.
He made his intentions clear from the first ball of final tour match. He launched the Indian innings with a four off Zimbabwe captain and all-rounder Sikandar Raza and reached 50 from 31 balls.
The teen fell off the final ball of the 14th over. Sooryavanshi was out off a Wessly Madhevere delivery when Brad Evans dashed from the ropes to long off and caught the ball.
Wicketkeeper Ishan Kishan (29), a half centurion on Saturday, did best among the other Indian batters, slamming four fours before being bowled by Raza.
Zimbabwe slumped to 65-4 in reply with opener Brian Bennett and Raza both dismissed for golden ducks. The highlight of the innings was a 60-run fifth-wicket stand between Burl and Madhevere (28).

item.title: What Hefazat seeks to achieve with Qawmi-based parties, why Jamaat has doubts
item.description:
Doubts have emerged regarding the future of the 11-party alliance led by Bangladesh Jamaat-e-Islami. Khelafat Majlis, an important ally, has decided not to participate in the alliance’s future programmes. Prior to this, Bangladesh Khelafat Andolan has also taken the same decision.

Meanwhile, discussions have sparked across the political arena regarding an initiative led by Hefazat-e-Islam Bangladesh to form a new coalition featuring seven Qawmi-based Islamic parties.

However, leaders of the involved parties maintain that it is premature to conclude that the 11-party alliance is dissolving or that a new political coalition is officially being formed.

Jamaat also claims that while Khelafat Majlis and Bangladesh Khelafat Andolan are not participating in joint programmes, they remain within the alliance.

Discontent within Khelafat Majlis—led by Maulana Abdul Basit Azad and Ahmad Abdul Kader—regarding the 11-party alliance is not new. Ahead of the 13th parliamentary election, dissatisfaction brewed over seat-sharing arrangements and a perceived lack of concessions regarding reserved seats for women in parliament.

Their primary grievance is that the Bangladesh Khelafat Majlis, led by Maulana Mamunul Haque, was given greater priority within the coalition. Additionally, suspicions that Jamaat might contest the upcoming local government elections independently further fuelled their grievances.

Khelafat Majlis advocates for alliance coordination in local elections as well. Against this backdrop, the party’s Central Majlis-e-Shura from its third general session on Saturday decided to step back from the 11-party alliance's joint activities. However, the party noted that it would remain open to broader unity in the future if required for the nation, its people, or Islam.

Discontent within Khelafat Majlis—led by Maulana Abdul Basit Azad and Ahmad Abdul Kader—regarding the 11-party alliance is not new. Ahead of the 13th parliamentary election, dissatisfaction brewed over seat-sharing arrangements and a perceived lack of concessions regarding reserved seats for women in parliament.

Ahmad Ali Quashemi, Naib-e-Ameer of Khelafat Majlis, told Prothom Alo that his party will henceforth conduct its programmes independently. Leaders from other parties may attend and speak at these events, and Khelafat leaders reserve the right to participate in other parties' events if they choose.

When asked about the seven-party unity initiative led by Hefazat-e-Islam, Kasemi stated that the process has not been finalised.

Earlier in June, Bangladesh Khelafat Andolan withdrew from the 11-party coalition's activities, requesting that its name no longer be used in alliance announcements.

Party sources indicated that the decision was driven by an inability to reach a seat-sharing consensus with Jamaat during the parliamentary election, as well as uncertainty surrounding the establishment of an upper house of parliament.

Maulana Habibullah Miyaji, Ameer of Bangladesh Khelafat Andolan, mentioned that should a new coalition form under the oversight of senior Hefazat scholars, his party would consider joining it.

Discussions surrounding a broader alliance among Islamic parties gained traction following the 2024 mass uprising. Initially, an eight-party platform emerged, including Jamaat-e-Islami and Islami Andolan Bangladesh. It later expanded into an 11-party coalition with the inclusion of the National Citizen Party (NCP), AB Party, and LDP.
